Et quia Ecclesiae Catholicae species plurimum erat obscurata à fraterculis quibusdam, qui summum[?] Pontificem pro Ecclesia iactabant, sententiam suam, imo Ecclesiae subiungit his verbis: A propria vocabuli significatione recedendum ipse non putarim, vt ea proprie principalissimeq; sancta Ecclesia Catho-lica diceretur, qua omnes recte & Apostolicae fidei, & non fictae charitatis homines complectatur. Docet idem, multos Papas errasse. Et sententiam ex Baldo adducit: Non debet quis dicere, credo id, quod credit Papa, sed illud, quod credit Ecclesia.
units.tr: I will say openly how things stand. Bernard raised the jurisdiction of the Roman Pontiff far above all the earlier Fathers, and it is for this reason that Bellarmine calls him a Papist. For Cyprian, Augustine, Ambrose, and the other earlier writers restrained the jurisdiction of the Roman Pontiff. Bernard, however, fell into those fatal times beyond the year one thousand, when Satan was already loosed. Therefore what he could not restrain, he bore as best he could. For after the year one thousand, many holy men, unable to restrain the Pope's jurisdiction in spiritual matters, bore it patiently. And to this day the Church of God would perhaps have shown the same patience, had two things not stood in the way: a plain change of doctrine at the Council of Trent, and a new step added to the jurisdiction, unheard of by the ancients, namely the Pope's principate in temporal matters. For we do not judge those to be Papists, or men to be condemned, who wish some jurisdiction of the Pope in spiritual matters to be acknowledged. Rather, we mean those who bend so far in obedience to the Pope that, along with a change of doctrine, they profess the Pope's jurisdiction in temporal matters, whether directly or indirectly; who follow this profession to the ruin of princes and the overthrow of commonwealths; and who show themselves Papists, that is, not patiently bearing the Pope's spiritual jurisdiction but fighting for a temporal jurisdiction, and in this cause proving themselves bold, rebellious, impious, bloodthirsty, and murderous parricides, so that they may establish this jurisdiction in temporal affairs. Those who teach that these things are to be done, who approve things done, or who do them themselves, we call Papists. Bernard was not such a man. The opinion of the Fathers about the Catholic Church was first altered by the little friars, but the ancient opinion against the little friars was admirably defended by pious and learned men in the Roman Church. Pico della Mirandola, in his book on faith and the order of believing, reports a view of the Church quite different from that which the Jesuits put forward. He proves that the determination of the Pope alone in matters of faith binds no one, following the opinion of Gerson, Scotus, Panormitanus, and the Cardinal of Cambrai, Theorem 8. And because the form of the Catholic Church had been greatly obscured by certain little friars, who boasted that the supreme Pontiff was the Church, he adds his own opinion, indeed the Church's, in these words: "I would not think one should depart from the proper meaning of the word, so that the holy Catholic Church would be called, properly and principally, that which embraces all men of right apostolic faith and not feigned charity." He teaches the same, that "many Popes have erred." And he cites an opinion from Baldus: "One ought not to say, 'I believe what the Pope believes,' but 'I believe what the Church believes.'"

units.la: Hactenus Ecclesiae Catholicae descriptionem audiuimus è Scripturis Patribusque[?]. Certum igitur est ex Ecclesiae consensu, Romanam non esse Catholicam. Non est sancta, non Catholica. Sequitur, ut dicamus de communione sanctorum.
units.tr: Thus far we have heard the description of the Catholic Church from Scripture and the Fathers. It is therefore certain from the consent of the Church that the Roman Church is not Catholic. She is neither holy nor Catholic. It follows that we should speak of the communion of saints.

units.la: CAPVT VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: Credo sanctorum communionem,
units.tr: I believe in the communion of saints,

units.la: COmmunio sanctorum significat societatem noui populi, qua qui sunt membra Ecclesiæ, ministerio Propheticæ & Apostolicæ doctrinæ, & Sacramentorum, in vnum corpus vocati sunt. Continet autem communionem cum capite Christo, & membrorum inter se, & communionem seu participationem omnium Christi beneficiorum. De qua communione Iohannes ait: Quod vidimus, & audiuimus, annunciamus vobis, vt & vos communionem habeatis nobiscum, & communio nostra fit cum Patre, & cum Filio eius Iesu Christo. Continet etiam dis[?]ibutionem donorum specialium, & obligationem membrorum, vt conferant omnia sua dona ad gloriam capitis sui Christi, atque ad salutem totius corporis, & quorumlibet inter se membrorum. Nec vltra extenditur hæc communio, quam vt eam sancti habeant, vel cum capite, vel inter se, nec impii hanc communionem inter se habere possunt, nec sancti cum impiis. Nam quod consortium iu-stitiæ cum iniustitia? & quæ communio luci cum tenebris? Quæ concordia Christi cum Belial? aut quæ portio fideli cum infideli? & quæ consensio templo Dei cum simulacris? Nam vos estis templum Dei viuentis, sicut dixit Deus: Habitabo in eis, & ambulabo, & ero illorum Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus. Iohannes etiam diserte docet, homines malos & impuros non habere hanc communionem. {a}Si dixerimus, nos communionem habere cum eo, & in tenebris incedimus, mentimur, & veritatem non facimus. Quod si in luce incedimus, sicut ipse est in luce, communionem habemus mutuam, & sanguis Iesu Christi filij eius purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: The communion of saints signifies the fellowship of the new people, by which those who are members of the Church are called into one body through the ministry of the prophetic and apostolic teaching and of the sacraments. It contains, moreover, communion with Christ the head, communion of the members among themselves, and the communion or participation in all the benefits of Christ. John speaks of this communion: "That which we have seen and heard we declare to you, that you also may have communion with us; and our communion is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ." It also contains the distribution of special gifts and the obligation of the members to contribute all their gifts to the glory of their head Christ, and to the salvation of the whole body and of each of the members among themselves. This communion extends no further than that the saints have it either with the head or among themselves; nor can the wicked have this communion among themselves, nor the saints with the wicked. "For what fellowship has righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion has light with darkness? What concord has Christ with Belial? or what portion has a believer with an unbeliever? and what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God, as God said: I will dwell in them, and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people." John also teaches plainly that evil and impure men do not have this communion. {a} "If we say that we have communion with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not do the truth. But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have mutual communion, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin."

units.la: {a} Ioh.1.6. [?] cato. Hæc communio sanctorum ita est propria, & peculiaris Ecclesiæ, ut sine ea Ecclesia non possit consistere. Siue enim invisibilem Ecclesiam, siue visibilem quæras, nec breuius, nec certius innotescit, quam ex communione sanctorum. Quamuis enim in Ecclesia visibili malos semper habeamus bonis commistos: societas tamen illa, quam habent mali inter se, quamuis in Ecclesia sint, nunquam dicitur sanctorum communio. Sed hoc peculiariter semper refertur ad illam societatem, quæ in Ecclesia est sanctis cum suo capite, & inter se. Nam per unum Spiritum nos omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus, inquit Apostolus, siue Iudæi, siue Græci, siue serui, siue liberi, & omnes una potione potati sumus in unum spiritum. Quia igitur hæc communio facta est per Spiritum sanctum, non potest esse inter impios, in quibus non est Spiritus sanctus. Denique est communio sanctorum, qui ergo non sunt sancti, non habent hanc communionem.
units.tr: {a} John 1:6. [?] cleanses. This communion of saints is so proper and peculiar to the Church that the Church cannot exist without it. For whether you seek the invisible Church or the visible, it is made known no more briefly and no more certainly than through the communion of saints. For although in the visible Church we always have the wicked mingled with the good, that fellowship which the wicked have among themselves, although they are in the Church, is never called the communion of saints. But this is always referred peculiarly to that fellowship which exists in the Church between the saints and their head, and among themselves. For, as the Apostle says, "by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and we were all made to drink of one Spirit." Since therefore this communion is effected by the Holy Spirit, it cannot exist among the impious, in whom the Holy Spirit is not. In short, it is the communion of saints; those therefore who are not saints do not have this communion.

units.la: Hanc igitur dirigimus præscriptionem adversus Pontificios. Omnia membra Ecclesiæ sanctæ Catholicæ habent communionem sanctorum cum Capite, & inter se. Sed nulla membra Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ habent hanc communionem cum Capite, & inter se: ergo nulla membra Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ sunt membra Ecclesiæ sanctæ Catholicæ. Excitasse videor crabrones istos. Imo vero clamabunt, inter aliqua membra Ecclesiæ nostræ potest esse communio sanctorum, quamuis inter malos, qui fidem Christi verbis profitentur, factis vero negant, non fit hæc communio. Atqui non sic effugere possunt. Nam communio hæc est communio sanctorum, quam omnes sancti habent cum Capite, & inter se. Cum Capite, per fidem; inter se per charitatem, per Spiritum sanctum. Omnes sancti habent hanc communionem, soli sancti habent: quia qui in tenebris ambulant, & dicunt, se habere hanc societatem, mentiuntur. Si soli sancti habent, non potest esse inter eos, in quibus nulla est interna virtus: hoc est, non potest esse inter membra Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ. Nam per hanc communionem, id est, per Spiritus sancti vinculum, neque mali inter se cohærent, neque mali cum bonis. Soli ergo boni & sancti hoc vinculo Spiritus cohærent cum Capite, & inter se. Cum Capite dico, non cum Diabolo, non cum Antichristo. Nam qui Diabolo aut Antichristo cohærent, quomodo Christo cohærere possunt? Nam quæ concordia Christo cum Belial? Inter se autem sancti cohærent, non cum mundo. Quare non cum mundo? Quia Christus dicit: Ego pro eis oro, non pro mundo oro; sed pro eis, quos mihi dedisti, quia tui sunt. Quibus verbis docet Dominus, inter quos sit communio sanctorum, & inter quos non sit. Nam illi omnes, pro quibus Christus non orat, non habent hanc communionem cum Christo: quia hoc est communionis nostræ magnum priuilegium, vt Christum habeamus communem intercessorem pro nobis apud Patrem. Ecclesia igitur in communione sanctorum non habet communionem cum mundo. Mundus autem quid est, nisi mali homines in mundo, qui nullam habent internam virtutem. Ecclesia igitur, quæ non est ex mundo, sed in mundo, non habet communionem cum malis, qui non sunt ex Ecclesia, sed in Ecclesia. Et mali isti, qui sunt ex mundo, quamuis sint cum bonis in externa societate permisti, non tamen habent communionem cum sanctis in Ecclesia.
units.tr: We therefore direct this prescription against the Papists. All members of the holy Catholic Church have communion of saints with the Head and among themselves. But no members of the Papist Church have this communion with the Head and among themselves: therefore no members of the Papist Church are members of the holy Catholic Church. I seem to have stirred up these hornets. Indeed they will cry out that among some members of our Church there can be communion of saints, although among wicked men who profess Christ's faith in words but deny it in deeds this communion does not arise. But they cannot escape in this way. For this communion is the communion of saints, which all saints have with the Head and among themselves. With the Head, through faith; among themselves, through love, through the Holy Spirit. All saints have this communion, only saints have it: because those who walk in darkness and say that they have this fellowship lie. If only saints have it, it cannot exist among those in whom there is no inner virtue; that is, it cannot exist among the members of the Papist Church. For through this communion, that is, through the bond of the Holy Spirit, neither the wicked cohere among themselves nor the wicked with the good. Only the good and holy therefore cohere with the Head and among themselves by this bond of the Spirit. With the Head I say, not with the Devil, not with Antichrist. For those who cohere with the Devil or Antichrist, how can they cohere with Christ? For what concord has Christ with Belial? Now the saints cohere among themselves, not with the world. Why not with the world? Because Christ says: "I pray for them; I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, because they are yours." By these words the Lord teaches between whom there is the communion of saints and between whom there is not. For all those for whom Christ does not pray do not have this communion with Christ: because it is the great privilege of our communion that we have Christ as our common intercessor with the Father for us. The Church therefore in the communion of saints has no communion with the world. But what is the world, except wicked men in the world, who have no inner virtue? The Church, therefore, which is not of the world but in the world, does not have communion with the wicked, who are not of the Church but in the Church. And those wicked men who are of the world, although they are mingled with the good in external society, nevertheless do not have communion with the saints in the Church.

units.la: Redeamus iam ad membra illa Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ, in quibus docent illi, nullam esse internam virtutem, sed tantum externam fidei professionem, & Sacramentorum communionem, quæ sensu ipso percipitur. Hæc sunt, inquiunt, partes & membra Ecclesiæ? At cuius Ecclesiæ? Respondent, Ecclesiam unam esse, non duas: ac proinde loqui eos necesse est de membris Ecclesiæ unius & veræ. Atqui hæc membra Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ non habent communionem cum Christo: non sunt ergo membra Ecclesiæ Christi. Cuius ergo Ecclesiæ membra sint, respondeant illi, qui suam Ecclesiam in ista præcipitia coniecerunt, ut velint nolint, ex suis ipsorum principiis, licet nobis multum reclamantibus, & cum multa commiseratione, & charitate renitentibus, & verbi lucem præferentibus, & sedulo monentibus, ut ab his sibi caveant præcipitiis: ruunt tamen, tanquam homines sur-di, & caeci, neque aliud caput offendere possunt Ecclesiae suae, cum quo communionem habent membra illa, quae sunt sine interna virtute, quam vel Diabolum, vel Antichristum. Nec alios fratres istius communionis, quam homines profanos ex hoc mundo, pro quibus Christus non interpellat Patrem.
units.tr: Let us now return to those members of the Papist Church in whom those men teach that there is no inner virtue, but only an external profession of faith and communion in the sacraments, which is perceived by the senses themselves. "These," they say, "are the parts and members of the Church." But of which Church? They reply that the Church is one, not two; and therefore they must of necessity speak of the members of the one and true Church. Yet these members of the Papist Church do not have communion with Christ: they are therefore not members of the Church of Christ. Let those men say whose members they are, who have plunged their Church into those precipices, so that, whether they will or no, from their own principles—though we strongly protest, and resist with much compassion and charity, and set before them the light of the Word, and diligently warn them to beware of these precipices—they nevertheless rush headlong, like deaf and blind men, and can find no other head of their Church with whom those members, who are without inner virtue, have communion, than the Devil or Antichrist. Nor can they find other brethren of this communion than profane men of this world, for whom Christ does not intercede with the Father.

units.la: Quid ergo? dicet mihi forte quispiam: negas in Ecclesia Romana esse sanctos? Non nego. Sed illud affirmare ausim[?], ex Pontificiorum principiis, sanctos, qui sunt in illa Ecclesia, non habere communionem cum illa Ecclesia, ac proinde Ecclesiam illam esse Ecclesiam homine, non re, Ecclesiam falsam, talem scilicet, qualem vocat Bellarminus, Ecclesiam malignantium, & synagogam Satanae; quae est congregatio eorum, qui nolunt discere, & quum audiunt veritatem, nolunt acquiescere. Quis autem negare potest, esse in illa Ecclesia aliquos sanctos, quum exeuntes ex ea sanctos viros quotidie Ecclesia Catholica in suo gremio excipiat? Et quis affirmare potest, san-ctos, id est, Christi membra habere communionem cum mundo, cum membris Satanae, in quibus nulla est interna virtus, sed externa tantum professio, & Sacramentorum communio, quae sensu ipso percipitur?
units.tr: What then? Someone may perhaps say to me: do you deny that there are saints in the Roman Church? I do not deny it. But I would dare to affirm this, from the principles of the Papists: the saints who are in that Church do not have communion with that Church, and therefore that Church is a Church in name, not in reality, a false Church, such as Bellarmine calls the Church of the malignant, and the synagogue of Satan, which is the assembly of those who will not learn, and when they hear the truth, will not give assent. Yet who can deny that there are some saints in that Church, since the Catholic Church daily receives into her bosom holy men coming out of it? And who can affirm that saints, that is, members of Christ, have communion with the world, with members of Satan, in whom there is no inner virtue, but only an external profession and communion in the sacraments, which is perceived by the senses themselves?

units.la: Testimonia Patrum de hac re peculiaria adhibere non est necesse: quia quaecunque testimonia probant, membra Ecclesiae non esse, nisi sanctos (de qua re consensum veteris Ec[?]clesiæ supra adduximus) probant etiam communionem hanc esse inter solos sanctos, non inter eos, in quibus nulla est virtus interna. Deinde, quæcunque probant Christum[?] esse Caput Ecclesiæ, Ecclesiam vero corpus eius, confirmant hanc communionem inter sanctos esse tantum: quia, urait[?] Irenæus, dicere; membra Christi non participare salutem, sed in perditionem redigi, quomodo non maxima est blasphemia? Blasphemi igitur sunt Iesuitæ, qui in membris Ecclesiæ, quæ sunt eadem & membra Christi, nullam internam requirunt virtutem.
units.tr: There is no need to adduce special testimonies of the Fathers on this matter, because whatever testimonies prove that only the saints are members of the Church (a point on which we have already cited the consensus of the ancient Church above) also prove that this communion is among the saints alone, not among those in whom there is no inward virtue. Moreover, whatever testimonies prove that Christ is the Head of the Church and the Church his body, confirm that this communion is only among the saints; for, as Irenaeus says, "to say that the members of Christ do not partake of salvation but are brought to perdition, how is this not the greatest blasphemy?" The Jesuits, therefore, are blasphemers, who in the members of the Church, which are the same as the members of Christ, require no inward virtue.

units.la: Quum igitur Ecclesia Pontificia, quæ pro-fitetur, se communionem habere cum improbis, reprobis, cum illis, in quibus nulla est interna virtus, communionem cum Christo habere non possit, inter membra Christi non sit; quid amplius de Ecclesia litem nobis moueant? Probent, apud se esse Ecclesiam sanctam, sanctorum communionem: probent, se esse in Corpore Christi, membra Christi: & vel respondeant ad vnanimem consensum Patrum de sanctitate membrorum: vel nouis expunctionibus expurgent antiquos Patres. Quamdiu enim hæc testimonia in Ecclesia extabunt, Ecclesia Pontificia nunquam vel sancta habebitur, vel Catholica, vel sanctorum communionis particeps.
units.tr: Since, then, the Papist Church, which professes that it has communion with the wicked, the reprobate, and those in whom there is no inward virtue, cannot have communion with Christ and is not among the members of Christ, why do they still stir up disputes with us about the Church? Let them prove that the Church is holy among them and that they have the communion of saints; let them prove that they are in the Body of Christ, as members of Christ; and let them either answer the unanimous consent of the Fathers concerning the holiness of the members, or purge the ancient Fathers by novel deletions. For as long as these testimonies stand in the Church, the Papist Church will never be held either holy, or Catholic, or a partaker of the communion of saints.

units.la: CAPUT VIII. De vnitate Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, quam n[?]retinet Ecclesia Pontificia.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII. On the unity of the Catholic Church, which the Papist Church does not retain.

units.la: Ecclesiæ vnitas in sacris Scripturis frequenter nobis commendata est, vt sine ea cognoscamus, nihil nobis consortii esse cum Christo & Ecclesia: quia Christo & Ecclesiæ eius, nihil est consortii cum malis hominibus, in quibus regnat Diabolus: quales sunt omnes, qui nullam habent internam virtutem. Quærendum ergo est, in quibus hæc Ecclesiæ vnitas consistat. Primum est, vt omnis Ecclesia vnum habeat Caput, nempe Christum. Hanc vnitatem Pontificii ruperunt, aliud caput ponendo: nec diuisionem istorum, & separationem ab Ecclesia Catholica saluare potest commentum ipsorum, de Capite ministeriali.
units.tr: The unity of the Church is commended to us frequently in the holy Scriptures, so that we may recognise that without it we have no fellowship with Christ and the Church. For Christ and his Church have no fellowship with wicked men, in whom the Devil reigns, and such are all who have no inward virtue. We must therefore ask in what this unity of the Church consists. The first point is that every Church has one Head, namely Christ. The Papists have broken this unity by setting up another head. Nor can their invention of a ministerial Head save the division and separation of those men from the Catholic Church.

units.la: Nam Ecclesia Catholica non habet vnitatem in aliquo vno capite ministeriali. Nos vnitatem quærimus Ecclesiæ Catholicæ; Caput ministeriale diuisionem probat, non vnitatem: quia omnis Ecclesia Catholica nunquam habuit hoc Caput. Orientales Ecclesiæ, & Australes non agnoscunt Romanum Pontificem Ecclesiæ Caput. Etsi rectè Bellarminus Catholicam Ecclesiam doceat complecti omnia tempora, omnia loca, omnes nationes: certè Papam excludit, ne possit esse Caput, ne quidem ministeriale Ecclesiæ Catholicæ: quia erant quædam tempora, & loca, & nationes, in quibus Ecclesia fuit, antequam Romanus quisquam Episcopus constitutus esset. Nam Catholica ex duobus populis facta est, Iudæis ac gentibus. Quia ipse est pax nostra, qui utraq; fe-cit unum, & intergermi[?] parietis septum solvit, inimicitias in carne sua, legem mandatorum in vitibus[?] evacuavit, ut ex duobus in semetipso conderet no-num hominem, faciens pacem. Ad hanc igitur uni-tatem pertinet pars illa, quæ stante adhuc medio illo pariete in Christum venturum credidit, & per fidem Christi salutem adepta est. Nam ex duobus in seipso unum fecit, non in alio. Solus ergo Christus est Ecclesiæ Catholicæ Caput, qui ante omnes erat. Nec erant tempora, aut loca, aut nationes, in quibus Ecclesia non agnouerit unum Christum, Caput, ac Dominum. Nec solum Catholica hoc unicum Caput agnoscit: sed & particulares Ecclesiæ suis locis distinctæ, unitatem cum Catholica retinentes, idem agnoscunt Caput. Paulus enim ad Ecclesiam Corinthiacam scribens, quæ particularis erat: Despondi, inquit, vos, uni viro, virginem castam exhibere Christo. Sin-gulæ igitur Ecclesiæ unum Caput agnoscunt, unum sponsum: qui aliud Caput, alium sponsum statuunt, unitatem Catholicæ Ecclesiæ rumpunt, sicut faciunt Pontificij.
units.tr: For the Catholic Church does not have unity in any one ministerial head. We are seeking the unity of the Catholic Church; a ministerial head proves division, not unity, because the whole Catholic Church never had this Head. The Eastern and Southern Churches do not acknowledge the Roman Pontiff as the Head of the Church. Although Bellarmine rightly teaches that the Catholic Church embraces all times, all places and all nations, he certainly excludes the Pope from being the Head of the Catholic Church, not even a ministerial one, because there were certain times, places and nations in which the Church existed before any Roman bishop had been appointed. For the Catholic Church was made up of two peoples, Jews and Gentiles. For he is our peace, who has made both one, and has broken down the middle wall of partition, the enmity in his flesh, abolishing the law of commandments in ordinances, that he might create in himself of twain one new man, making peace. To this unity therefore belongs that part which, while the dividing wall still stood, believed that Christ would come and obtained salvation through faith in Christ. For he made the two into one in himself, not in another. Christ alone, then, who was before all, is the Head of the Catholic Church. Nor were there times, places or nations in which the Church did not acknowledge the one Christ as Head and Lord. Nor does the Catholic Church alone acknowledge this one Head: the particular Churches, distinguished by their own places and retaining unity with the Catholic Church, acknowledge the same Head. For Paul, writing to the Corinthian Church, which was a particular church, says: I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. Each Church therefore acknowledges one Head, one bridegroom. Those who set up another head and another bridegroom break the unity of the Catholic Church, as the Papists do.

units.la: Secundo una etiam dicitur Ecclesia Catholica ab unitate corporis. Sicut enim corpus unum est, inquit Apostolus, & membra habet multa, omnia vero membra corporis unum, multa quum sint, unum sunt corpus, ita & Christus. Hic est Christus mysticus, non mystica Ecclesia: nam vera est Ecclesia, & propria. Non enim aliam Ecclesiam vspiam describit nobis Apostolus, quam vnam illam, veram, & propriam, quam vocat Corpus Christi. Ab hac vnitate, sua confessione, decidunt Pontificii: quia in membris Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ non requiritur vlla interna virtus. Membra autem, quæ sunt sine fide & charitate, non possunt retinere vnitatem huius corporis, quia totum corpus à capite, secundum mensuram uniuscuiusq; membri, incrementum capit corporis conuniens[?], ad ædificationem sui per charitatem. Itaque cuius Ecclesiæ membra per fidem & charitatem non retinent vnitatem huius corporis: decidunt ab vnitate corporis: At Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ membra sunt huiusmodi: Decidunt igitur ab vnitate corporis.
units.tr: Secondly, the Catholic Church is also called one from the unity of the body. For as the body is one, says the Apostle, and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so also is Christ. This is the mystical Christ, not a mystical Church: for the Church is true and proper. Indeed the Apostle describes to us no other Church anywhere than that one true and proper Church, which he calls the Body of Christ. By their own confession the Papists fall away from this unity, because in the members of the Papist Church no inward virtue is required. But members who are without faith and charity cannot retain the unity of this body, because from the Head the whole body, fitly joined together and knit together, through every joint of supply, according to the working in due measure of every part, makes the increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love. Therefore, whichever Church's members do not through faith and charity retain the unity of this body, they fall away from the unity of the body. But the members of the Papist Church are of this kind. They therefore fall away from the unity of the body.

units.la: Deinde vna etiam dicitur Ecclesia, ab vnitate Spiritus, quo gubernatur & instituitur vniuersa Ecclesia. Apostolus scribens de donis ad ædificationem Ecclesiæ concessis. Hæc, inquit, omnia efficit vnus idemq; Spiritus. Eodemq; Spiritu docet omnia Ecclesiæ membra regi. Nam de omnibus Ecclesiæ membris dicit: Per vnum Spiritum nos omnes in vnum corpus baptizati sumus. Quibus verbis manifestum est, Apostolum non hærere in externa communione Sacramentorum, quæ sensu ipso percipitur, sed virtutem Sacramenti exponere. Quia enim per baptismatis gratiam regenerantur homines, & fiunt filii Dei; ideirco vnitas hæc, quam habet Ecclesia à Baptismatis Sacramento, non intelligitur externa ab Apostolo, sed interna & spiritualis; quia per unum Spiritum nos omnes baptizati sumus in unum corpus: hoc est, regeneramur, & in hoc sancto Ecclesiæ corpore membra efformamur. Itaque Apostolus tria coniungit, Unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma. Quasi dixisset: Unum Caput, una regula, unum corpus regeneratorum per baptisma. Ex ipsis Apostoli verbis, Baptisma non de externa communione, quæ sensu percipitur, sed de interna virtute regenerationis intelligere cogimur, quia Apostolus quasi explicans, quid per baptisma intelligat, dicit: Nos omnes per unum Spiritum baptizati sumus in unum corpus. Ab hac vero unitate Spiritus excussos esse Pontificios, sua confessio probat: quia in membris Ecclesiæ suæ internam Spiritus virtutem nullam requirunt. Omnia membra Ecclesiæ Catholicæ retinent hanc unitatem Spiritus, & ab uno Spiritu reguntur: At omnia membra Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ non tenent hanc Spiritus unitatem, nec ab uno Spiritu reguntur: Ecclesia igitur Pontificia non tenet hanc unitatem cum Ecclesia Catholica.
units.tr: Thirdly, the Church is also called one from the unity of the Spirit, by whom the whole Church is governed and instituted. The Apostle, writing about the gifts bestowed for the edifying of the Church, says: All these things are wrought by one and the same Spirit. He teaches that all the members of the Church are ruled by the same Spirit. For concerning all the members of the Church he says: By one Spirit we are all baptised into one body. By these words it is plain that the Apostle is not dwelling on the outward communion of the sacraments, which is perceived by the senses, but is setting out the power of the sacrament. For because men are regenerated by the grace of baptism and become sons of God, this unity which the Church has from the sacrament of Baptism is understood by the Apostle not as outward but as inward and spiritual, because by one Spirit we were all baptised into one body: that is, we are regenerated and formed as members in this holy body of the Church. Thus the Apostle joins three things: one Lord, one faith, one baptism. As if he had said: one Head, one rule, one body of those regenerated through baptism. From the Apostle's own words we are compelled to understand Baptism not as the outward communion perceived by the senses, but as the inward power of regeneration, since the Apostle, as if explaining what he means by baptism, says: we were all baptised by one Spirit into one body. That the Papists have been cast out from this unity of the Spirit is proved by their own confession, since they require no inward power of the Spirit in the members of their Church. All the members of the Catholic Church retain this unity of the Spirit and are governed by one Spirit; but all the members of the Papist Church do not hold this unity of the Spirit, nor are they governed by one Spirit. The Papist Church therefore does not hold this unity with the Catholic Church.

units.la: Una præterea dicitur Ecclesia Catholica, ab unitate fidei: de qua unitate dicit Apostolus: Unus Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma. Fides autem una dicitur, propter unitatem regulæ fidei, quam unam esse in Ecclesia Catholica, immobilem, inde-
units.tr: Furthermore, the Catholic Church is called one from the unity of faith, concerning which unity the Apostle says: One Lord, one faith, one baptism. Faith is called one on account of the unity of the rule of faith, which is one in the Catholic Church, unchangeable, and

units.la: [no further heading]
units.tr: [no further heading]

units.la: mutabilem ex superioris Ecclesiae consensu demonstrauimus. Ab hac autem unitate fidei ceciderunt Pontificii, quia hanc regulam in Concilio Tridentino mutarunt. Alteram enim regulae huius partem nouam, inauditam antea, commentitiam obtrudunt, traditiones scilicet quascunque probat Ecclesia Romana, quae nullam Scripturarum auctoritatem habent. Istas omnes nugas suas in regula fidei ponunt Pontificii. Regulam igitur mutarunt, imo vero & quotidie mutant. Nam qui semel ab unica Scripturarum regula deciderint, nunquam invenient, ubi sistere possunt; sed quotidie nova monstra excogitant, quae etiam ad fidem Catholicam referre non erubescunt. Ab unitate igitur fidei separaverunt se Pontificii, quum regulam illam unicam fidei mutarunt, quam ante ipsos Catholica Ecclesia tenuit semper immutatam, quamque deinceps etiam, quamvis ipsis furentibus & frementibus, eadem Ecclesia Catholica inviolatam retinebit usque ad adventum Domini.
units.tr: have shown from the consensus of the earlier Church that it is one, unchanging and not subject to alteration. The Papists have fallen away from this unity of faith, because at the Council of Trent they changed this rule. They have foisted on it a second part that is new and previously unheard of, an invented addition, namely all the traditions which the Roman Church approves, though these have no authority from the Scriptures. The Papists place all these trifles of theirs within the rule of faith. They have therefore changed the rule, indeed they change it every day. For those who have once fallen away from the single rule of the Scriptures will never find where they can stop; instead they devise new monsters every day, and do not blush to refer them even to the Catholic faith. The Papists have therefore separated themselves from the unity of faith when they changed that single rule of faith, which the Catholic Church held before them, always unchanged, and which the same Catholic Church will keep inviolate after them, until the coming of the Lord, although the Papists rage and rave against it.

units.la: Una ergo est Ecclesia Catholica, quia unum habet Caput, quia unum est corpus, quia uno Spiritu regitur, quia una fidei regula dirigitur. Ecclesia nunc Romana nec unum hoc Caput habet, nec in uno hoc corpore consistit, nec uno hoc Spiritu regitur, nec unica hac regula dirigitur: non ergo unitatem retinet cum Ecclesia Catholica. Sed haerent in capite: dicunt, Romanum Pontificem esse Caput minis-tenisteriale,& Christi Vicarium in tota Ecclesia. Caput ministeriale duo significat, ministrum, & dominum, quæ duo ita sunt diuersa, vt vni eodem respectu convenire non possint. Dicantur, vtrum Papa sit Ecclesiæ minister, an dominus. Si ministrum dicant: Respondeo, ministerium datum non vni alicui ad vniuersam Ecclesiam Catholicam, sed singulis pro mensura sua, ad singulas Ecclesiæ partes regendas. Nemo enim ministerium exercet in tota Ecclesia: quia membrum, naturam & mensuram membri excedere non potest. Monstrum igitur ex Ecclesia faciunt, qui Caput ministeriale, hoc est, membrum vnum ad omnia extendunt. Singuli Episcopi portionem suam in Catholica[?] retinent, nec quisquam mensuram membri excedere debet. Ita tamen isti in singulis partibus exercentur, vt quia partes inter se vinculo pacis & vnitatis cohærent, tanquam vnius corporis partes, quicquid agunt in sua parte (quamdiu vnitatem hanc retinuerint, de qua diximus) non tantum pro se, verum etiam pro tota[?] Ecclesia agere existimantur. Itaque multi Episcopi vnum Episcopatum constituunt. Pulchre Cyprianus: Nemo fraternitatem mendacio fallat, nemo fidei veritatem perfida prævaricatione corrumpat. Episcopatus vnus est, cuius a singulis in solidum pars tenetur. Cyprianus Romani Pontificis vanitatem, & mendacii & perfidiæ prævaricationis nomine grauiter coarguit, qui ausus fuerat hanc Episcoporum vnitatem violare. EpiEpiscopi igitur singuli in suis partibus ministerium exercendo, capita ministerialia quodammodo dici possunt; qui autem ultra partem suam ministerium extendit, non iam ministerium, sed dominatum quaerit. Atq; hinc Romanae sese produnt fallaciae, quod, dum ministerium prætendunt, dominatum quaeritur. Dominum autem Ecclesiae Catholicae unum tantummodo agnoscimus Christum; sicut docet Apostolus: Unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma. Hinc ergo apparet, Tridentinos Ecclesiae Caput mutasse, qui Romanum Caput Ecclesiae Catholicae imponunt. Deinde Rom. Pontifex Caput est eorum, qui nullam habent internam virtutem, teste Bellarmino: At Christus Caput est sanctorum. Duas ergo Ecclesias fingunt Pontificii, unam eorum, qui sancti sunt, cuius Ecclesiae Caput est Christus: aliam eorum, qui impii sunt, cuius Ecclesiae Caput est Rom. Pontifex, si Iesuitæ verum docent. Ita Rom. Pontifex nec potest esse Caput ministeriale sub Christo, nec Vicarius Christi: quia Vicarius est, non qui res alienas, sed qui res domini sui curat, a domino ad hoc constitutus. Papa autem, qui regit Ecclesiam, cuius membra sunt homines impii, Iesuitarum iudicio; nec minister, nec Vicarius Christi esse potest; quia non regit Ecclesiam sanctorum sub Christo, sed aliam, non curat res domini sui, sed alienas. Ecclesia igitur Romana, quae aliud habet Caput, alium dominum, alium spiritum, alia membra, non potest esse Ecclesia Christi, quæ ideo vna dicitur, quia vnum habet Caput, vnum Dominum, vnum Spiritum: Vnum est corpus, vnam habet fidei regulam.
units.tr: The Catholic Church is therefore one, because it has one Head, because it is one body, because it is ruled by one Spirit, and because it is directed by one rule of faith. The Roman Church now has neither this one Head, nor does it stand in this one body, nor is it ruled by this one Spirit, nor is it directed by this single rule. It therefore does not keep unity with the Catholic Church. But they cling to the Head. They say that the Roman Pontiff is the ministerial Head and the Vicar of Christ in the whole Church. A ministerial head signifies two things, a minister and a lord, and these two are so different that they cannot belong to one and the same person in the same respect. Let them say whether the Pope is the minister of the Church or its lord. If they say minister, I answer: the ministry was not given to one man for the whole Catholic Church, but to each man according to his measure, for governing the individual parts of the Church. For no one exercises a ministry over the whole Church, because a member cannot exceed the nature and measure of a member. Those therefore make a monster of the Church who extend one member, that is, the ministerial head, over everything. Each bishop keeps his own portion within the Catholic Church, and no one ought to exceed the measure of a member. Yet these men are so exercised in their individual parts that, since the parts cohere with one another by the bond of peace and unity, like the parts of one body, whatever they do in their own part (so long as they keep that unity of which we have spoken) is considered to be done not only for themselves but for the whole Church. Hence many bishops constitute one episcopate. Cyprian well says: Let no one deceive the brotherhood with a lie, let no one corrupt the truth of the faith by faithless prevarication. The episcopate is one, and each bishop holds a part of it in its entirety. Cyprian sharply condemns the vanity of the Roman Pontiff under the name of lie and faithless prevarication, since he had dared to violate this unity of the bishops. Each bishop, then, exercising a ministry in his own part, can in a certain sense be called a ministerial head; but whoever extends his ministry beyond his own part no longer seeks a ministry but lordship. And here the Roman deceits are revealed: while they put forward a ministry, they are seeking a lordship. We, however, acknowledge only one Lord of the Catholic Church, Christ; as the Apostle teaches: one Lord, one faith, one baptism. From this it therefore appears that the Tridentines have changed the Head of the Church, since they impose the Roman Head on the Catholic Church. Next, the Roman Pontiff is the head of those who have no inward virtue, as Bellarmine testifies; but Christ is the Head of the saints. The Papists therefore invent two churches: one of those who are holy, whose Head is Christ; the other of those who are wicked, whose Head is the Roman Pontiff, if the Jesuits teach the truth. Thus the Roman Pontiff can be neither a ministerial head under Christ nor the Vicar of Christ, because a vicar is not one who looks after another's affairs, but one who looks after the affairs of his lord, appointed to this by the lord. But the Pope, who rules a Church whose members are, by the judgment of the Jesuits, wicked men, can be neither minister nor Vicar of Christ; because he does not rule the Church of the saints under Christ, but another church; he does not look after the affairs of his lord, but those of others. The Roman Church, therefore, which has another head, another lord, another spirit, and other members, cannot be the Church of Christ, which is called one because it has one Head, one Lord, one Spirit; it is one body, and has one rule of faith.

units.la: Sed quia externam fidei professionem obtinere se existimant Pontificii, & Sacramentorum communionem, quæ sensu ipso percipitur: examinanda est etiam hæc vnitas, quæ in externa professione consistit. Nam si ab hoc etiam vnitatis consortio deciderint Pontificii, penitus ab vnitate excederunt; quia hæc est tantummodo vnitas illa, quam illi se habere profitentur. Nam in definitione Ecclesiæ, tantummodo externam professionem, & Romani Pontificis regimen agnoscunt. Apostolus dicit, vnum esse dominum, vnam fidem, vnum baptisma. Si vna fides exponitur, vna fidei professio, verba intelligenda erunt de regula fidei; quam vnicam esse, supra docuimus. Ac proinde vnitatem Ecclesiæ Catholicæ in externa professione retinere non possunt, qui vnicam fidei regulam mutarunt: quia externa professio semper secundum regulam fidei dirigenda est. Regulam autem fidei, vnicam illam & immobilem antiquis, mutarunt Pontificii: & in Romani Pontificis potestate esse iactant, vt quotidie mutetur.
units.tr: But because the Papists think that they hold the external profession of faith and the communion of the sacraments, which are perceived by the senses itself, this unity, which consists in the external profession, must also be examined. For if the Papists have also fallen away from this fellowship of unity, they have departed entirely from unity, since this is only that unity which they profess to have. For in their definition of the Church they acknowledge only the external profession and the rule of the Roman Pontiff. The Apostle says that there is one Lord, one faith, one baptism. If one faith is taken to mean one profession of faith, the words must be understood of the rule of faith, which we have shown above to be single. And therefore those who have changed the single rule of faith cannot keep the unity of the Catholic Church in the external profession, because the external profession must always be directed according to the rule of faith. The Papists have changed the rule of faith, which was single and unchanging for the ancients, and they boast that it lies in the power of the Roman Pontiff to be changed every day.

units.la: Docent enim, {a}Ex arbitrio Romani Pontificis pendere, decreta fidei sancire, & sancita mutare. Regula igitur fidei Tridentinis[?] istis non est vnica, & semper eadem, atque immobilis: vnde sequitur, Ecclesiam nunc Romanam nō retinere vnitatem cum Catholica in externa fidei professione. Quid est igitur, quod isti offendere possunt, quod eos in Catholica retineat Ecclesia? non Capitis vnitas; quia aliud sibi Caput excogitarunt, alium dominum, alium sponsum: non membrorum & corporis vnitas, quia n embra Ecclesiæ suæ homines profanos esse docent: non Spiritus vnitas, quam à se procul reiiciunt: non fidei vnitas, quam ipsi sua confessione quotidie mutant. Quis igitur demonstrare poterit, Romanam Ecclesiam cum Ecclesia Catholica vnitatem retinere?
units.tr: For they teach that {a}the decrees of faith depend on the judgment of the Roman Pontiff, to sanction them and to change what has been sanctioned. The rule of faith, therefore, for these Tridentines is not single, always the same, and unchanging; from which it follows that the present Roman Church does not keep unity with the Catholic Church in the external profession of faith. What, then, is there in them that could hold them in the Catholic Church? Not unity of Head, because they have devised for themselves another head, another lord, another bridegroom; not unity of members and body, because they teach that the members of their Church are profane men; not unity of Spirit, which they reject far from themselves; not unity of faith, which they change every day by their own confession. Who, then, will be able to show that the Roman Church keeps unity with the Catholic Church?

units.la: CAPVT IX. Vera Ecclesia optime cognoscitur ex ministerio suo, in conservanda regula fidei.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX. The true Church is best recognised by its ministry in keeping the rule of faith.

units.la: QUanquam ex iis, quæ hactenus disputavimus, vera Christi Ecclesia sine errore agnosci possit, quia tamen importuni homines hanc rem vehementius scribendo exagitant, ita ut infirmorum animi perturbentur, & in quærenda Ecclesia sese multum fatigent: ut horum infirmitati consulamus, alteram quæstionis, quam initio proposuimus, partem hoc loco tractabimus. Quæstio est, quomodo vera Ecclesia cognosci possit? Hoc illud est, quod passim quæritur. Sic enim dicunt: Si de vera Ecclesia certo constarer, cætera facilius componi possent. Nam Ecclesia est sine dubio audienda. Omnis autem hæsitatio est, ubinam sit Eccle-
units.tr: Although the true Church of Christ can be recognised without error from what we have argued so far, nevertheless, because troublesome men press this matter very hard in their writings, so that the minds of the weak are disturbed and they weary themselves greatly in seeking the Church, we will treat the second part of the question we proposed at the beginning, in order to relieve the weakness of these people. The question is: how can the true Church be known? This is what is asked everywhere. For people say: "If we were certain about the true Church, the rest could be settled more easily. For the Church is without doubt to be heard. But the whole difficulty is where the Church is."

units.la: Eccl Prot liæ c Quo num Dixi de C com mus quia lam rend R cuiss relig eclesi corum licite quæl regu smat nem sunt viola nost ficio gunt necr hom certa sit Ec tici? Ecclesia. Pontificii affirmant, apud se esse: Protestantes, qui vocantur, ad se pertinere: aliæ etiam sectæ Ecclesiæ nomine gloriantur. Quomodo igitur in tanta varietate opinionum cognoscetur, ubinam sit vera Ecclesia? Diximus de capite, de membris, de sanctitate, de Catholicorum dispersione, de sanctorum communione, de unitate. Restat, ut vera tractemus exactius, quæ ad regulam fidei pertinent, quia ex illa regula facile respondebimus ad illam quæstionem, qua quærunt [?], ubinam quærenda, & quomodo cognoscenda sit Ecclesia?
units.tr: The Papists affirm that the Church is with them; the Protestants, as they are called, claim it belongs to them; other sects also boast of the name of the Church. How, then, amid so great a variety of opinions, will it be known where the true Church is? We have spoken of the head, of the members, of holiness, of the dispersion of the Catholics, of the communion of the saints, and of unity. It remains that we treat more exactly what pertains to the rule of faith, because from that rule we will easily answer the question by which they ask where the Church is to be sought and how it is to be recognised.

units.la: Respondeo igitur, hanc quæstionem exercuisse antiquos Patres, in quorum vestigiis si religiose insistimus, non est dubium, quin Ecclesiam teneamus, quam inter varios hæreticorum errores, furores, terrores fortiter & feliciter tenuerant illi. Quoties enim de Ecclesia quæstio erat, probabant Patres Ecclesiam, per regulam charitatis contra schismaticos. Schismatici enim, qui externam fidei professionem tenuerunt, deiecti tamen ab Ecclesia sunt, quia charitatem atque unitatem Ecclesiæ violarunt. Sed dimissis schismaticis, omnis nostra contentio est contra hæreticos, Pontificios intelligo. At illi nobis vicissim [?] impingunt hæreseos notam. Verum nec ipsorum, nec nostris verbis credi volumus, quia omnes homines contentiosi sumus. Itaque regula certa est, quæ demonstrare potest, apud quos sit Ecclesia, tum quinam sint habendi hæretici?
units.tr: I answer, therefore, that the ancient Fathers dealt with this question. If we follow their footsteps devoutly, there is no doubt that we hold the Church which they held firmly and happily amid the various errors, rages and terrors of the heretics. For whenever the question of the Church arose, the Fathers proved the Church by the rule of charity against the schismatics. For the schismatics, though they held the outward profession of the faith, were nevertheless cast out of the Church, because they violated the charity and unity of the Church. But setting the schismatics aside, all our contention is against the heretics, I mean the Papists. Yet they in turn charge us with the mark of heresy. But we do not wish to be believed either on their word or on ours, since we are all contentious men. Therefore the rule is certain which can show where the Church is, and also who ought to be held heretics.

units.la: Si quæras igitur, quænam sit vera Ecclesia, breuissima est responsio, & verissima: Ecclesia vera est, quæ regulam fidei vnam, eandem, indemutabilem confessuar. Quum igitur docuerimus, hanc regulam fidei per omnes Ecclesiæ successiones fuisse agnitam, susceptam, celebratam, perpetuoque conseruatam vsque ad Concilii Tridentini tempora: Quumque constet, fuisse eandem regulam susceptam ab Ecclesiis reformatis, per quam regulam nostræ Ecclesiæ suam communionem probant cum Ecclesiis antiquis, cum Ecclesia denique Catholica: fuisse etiam hanc regulam à Pontificiis mutatam in pseudosynodo Tridentina: Quum hæc, inquam, constituerint, expedita via, ratioq; constabit inueniendi Ecclesiam, quam quærimus.
units.tr: If you ask, then, what the true Church is, the answer is very brief and very true: the true Church is that which confesses one, the same and unchangeable rule of faith. Since we have shown that this rule of faith has been acknowledged, received, observed and preserved without interruption through all the successions of the Church until the time of the Council of Trent; and since it is clear that the same rule was received by the reformed Churches, and by it our Churches prove their communion with the ancient Churches, and finally with the Catholic Church; and since this rule was changed by the Papists in the pseudo-synod of Trent: when these things, I say, are established, a plain way and a method of finding the Church we seek will be evident.

units.la: Regula fidei vel summaria est, vel completa, & perfectè explicata. Summaria regula est in Symbolo Apostolico. Itaque nonnulli Patres, quum regulam fidei proponunt, Symbolum explicant. Completa regula est doctrina Propherica & Apostolica in sacris Scripturis comprehensa; ac proinde multi Patres in regula fidei designanda, vniuersas Scripturas proponunt. Idemque habetur apud Patres, Ecclesiam probari per regulam fidei, & Ecclesiam probari per Scripturas. De qua re deinceps dicetur.
units.tr: The rule of faith is either summary or complete and perfectly explained. The summary rule is in the Apostles' Creed. Therefore some Fathers, when they set out the rule of faith, expound the Creed. The complete rule is the prophetic and apostolic doctrine comprehended in the holy Scriptures; and accordingly many Fathers, in designating the rule of faith, set forth the whole of the Scriptures. And the same is held among the Fathers: that the Church is proved by the rule of faith, and that the Church is proved by the Scriptures. This matter will be discussed below.

units.la: Miseri homines, & Scripturarum lucifugæ, ab Ecclesiæ Catholicæ societate per vitæ impuritatem deiecti, ipsam Scripturarum lucem exo frau prin cras ta in Cat fide Ecc fiam ptur perS lecta [?] Quu runt bitri Papa impr tiam & co Tr princ ca, & proc prop tesq; quor blicar tatem nefan tellig rium Qu
units.tr: Wretched men, enemies of the Scriptures, cast out from the society of the Catholic Church by the impurity of their lives, hate the very light of the Scriptures, and accuse them; by the Scriptures their frauds are uncovered and their malice is refuted. And first, either ignorantly or fraudulently, they attack the holy Scriptures; then, with open wickedness, they go on to rage against them.

units.la: fia, cle- em, do- Ec- am, [?]que que m ab no- bant ique Pon- enti- pedi- fiam, [illegible, ~3 letters] nple- ala est li Pa- mbo- strina pturis in re- pturas Patres, Eccle- edein- ifugæ, ita im- lucem exosam exosam ipsis, accusant; per quam ipsorum fraudes deteguntur, malitia reuincitur. Ac primo quidem vel inscite, vel fraudulenter sacras Scripturas impugnant: deinde vero aperta improbitate grassantur. Primo enim fidem Catholicam ab Ecclesia pendere volunt, vt ea fides Catholica habeatur, quamcunque docet Ecclesia. Secundo loco Scripturas & Ecclesiam committunt inter se, vbi statuunt, Scripturas per Ecclesiam probandas, non autem per Scripturas Ecclesiam. Tertio loco in proiectam audaciam & blasphemiam erumpunt. Quum enim de iudice controuersiarum quaerunt, non dubitant, sacras Scripturas Papae arbitrio subiicere; quamuis ipsorum iudicio, Papa vt plurimum sit homo vel indoctus, vel improbus. Nos vero tentabimus per Dei gratiam haec expedire, quae ab istis fraudulenter & confuse ponuntur.
units.tr: For first they want the Catholic faith to depend on the Church, so that whatever the Church teaches is held to be the Catholic faith. Secondly, they set the Scriptures and the Church against each other, where they lay down that the Scriptures are to be proved by the Church, and not the Church by the Scriptures. Thirdly, they break out into shameless audacity and blasphemy. For when they inquire about the judge of controversies, they do not hesitate to subject the holy Scriptures to the will of the Pope, although by their own judgement the Pope is for the most part either unlearned or wicked. But we will try, by the grace of God, to clear up these matters, which they put forward fraudulently and confusedly.

units.la: Tria sunt cognitionis Christianae tanquam principia: Fides Catholica, Ecclesia Catholica, & sacra Scriptura: quae in salute hominum procuranda, suum habent singula officium, proprium munus, atq; adeo stationem limitesq; suos. Tanta vero est Diaboli malitia, vt quorundam hominum improbitatem in publicam perniciem armatam producat, ad veritatem oppugnandam: ita vt haec tria inter se nefanda impietate collidant, quae si recte intelligantur, & sobrie tractentur, salutis mysterium continent, atq; aperiunt.
units.tr: There are three things, as it were principles, of Christian knowledge: the Catholic faith, the Catholic Church and the holy Scripture. Each of these has its own office, its proper function, and therefore its station and its limits, in procuring the salvation of men. But so great is the malice of the devil that he brings forth the wickedness of certain men, armed for public destruction, to assail the truth, so that these three things clash with one another in unspeakable impiety; though if they are rightly understood and soberly treated, they contain and open up the mystery of salvation.

units.la: Quod primo loco docens, fidem Catholiquam[?] illam esse, quamcunque docet Ecclesia: inscitiam, an fraudem appellem? Nam quomodo fides Catholica primum orbi innotuit? quomodo nata, orta, & in fidelibus suscepta est? nonne per Scripturarum prædicationem?
units.tr: Taking up the first point, the man who teaches that the Catholic faith is whatever the Church teaches: should I call this ignorance or fraud? For how did the Catholic faith first become known to the world? How was it born, arise, and get received among the faithful? Was it not by the preaching of the Scriptures?

units.la: Fides ex auditu, inquit Apostolus, auditus autem per verbum Dei. Fides ergo Catholica est ex verbo, & per verbum, non autem verbum per fidem, aut ex fide. At, inquiunt, fides est ab Ecclesia, nec alia est fides vera, nisi quam proponit, imo (ut isti volunt) quam ponit Ecclesia.
units.tr: "Faith comes by hearing," says the Apostle, "and hearing by the word of God." Therefore the Catholic faith is from the word, and through the word, and not the word through faith or from faith. But, they say, faith is from the Church, and no other faith is true except the one the Church sets forth; indeed (as they wish) the one the Church lays down.

units.la: Agite, ut veritas hic illustrius appareat, ponamus istos homines, qui fidem ab Ecclesiæ arbitrio pendere volunt, tum fuisse ubi nunc sunt, tum temporis vixisse, quando Apostoli Ecclesias per orbem terrarum collegerunt. Quando populus in tenebris sedebat, quando lux magna orta est iis, qui sederunt in tenebris, & in umbra mortis. Ecclesia erat colligenda ab Apostolis. Quomodo? Quid erat illud, quod populos ad Christum adduxit? nonne fides prædicata? Unde erat fides illa? ab Ecclesia, an à Deo? ab hominibus, an è cœlo? quis negat à Deo fuisse, atque è cœlo? Ergo populus ille, qui prius erat in tenebris, factus est Ecclesia Christi per fidem prædicatam. Ecclesia igitur pendet à fide, collecta est per fidem. Lux illa magna, quæ lucebat iis, qui in tenebris sedebant, quid est, nisi fides Catholica? Fides ergo Catholica, quæ populos è tenebris in Ecclesiam eduxit, est lux, & regula Ecclesiæ,
units.tr: Come now, that the truth may appear more clearly here, let us suppose those men who want faith to depend on the will of the Church to have been where they now are, and to have lived at the time when the Apostles gathered Churches throughout the world. When the people sat in darkness, when a great light arose for those who sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, the Church had to be gathered by the Apostles. How? What was it that brought the peoples to Christ? Was it not the faith preached? Whence was that faith? From the Church, or from God? From men, or from heaven? Who denies that it was from God and from heaven? Therefore that people, which before was in darkness, was made the Church of Christ through the faith preached. The Church therefore depends on faith; it was gathered through faith. That great light which shone for those who sat in darkness, what is it but the Catholic faith? Therefore the Catholic faith, which led the peoples out of darkness into the Church, is the light and the rule of the Church.

units.la: non forte in E mun præd Eccl ratio perse & co colle Eccl homi
units.tr: Not perhaps... in the world the preaching... the Church... the reasoning... in the world, by preaching, the Church was gathered... and men.

units.la: ligen ex co teft. Cathe cand lo, i propo
units.tr: ...to be understood... from... testimony... Catholic... perhaps... set forth...

units.la: Sec fe Eccl tenebr nem n neglig verbi tholic sed pr bulis lam, q nitus obtru non [?] autem Ecclesia regula fidei. Clamabunt forte tenebriones isti, hæc omnia vera esse in in Ecclesiæ initiis. Sed quomodo Ecclesia è mundo colligi primum potuit, nisi per fidem prædicatam? At aliam dicent rationem esse Ecclesiæ colligendæ, & iam collectæ: aliam rationem in plantatione Ecclesiarum, aliam in perfectione: fide Catholica vocari primum, & colligi Ecclesiam: sed quum iam vocata, & collecta fuerit, & in fide firmata, tum demum Ecclesiam debere fidem proponere, omnes homines ab Ecclesia fidem excipere.
units.tr: Secondly, the Church, when it was gathered from darkness, had the rule of faith before it; so these men, neglecting the word of God, ... the Catholic faith ... but the Church, having been brought into light, set forth the rule of faith, which was not forced upon it by human decrees ... Those men will perhaps cry out that all these things are true in the beginnings of the Church. But how could the Church first be gathered out of the world, except through the faith preached? But they will say that there is one way of gathering the Church, and another for a Church already gathered: one way in planting Churches, another in perfecting them; that the Church is first called and gathered by the Catholic faith, but when it has been called and gathered and established in the faith, then at last the Church ought to set forth the faith, and all men ought to receive the faith from the Church.

units.la: Respondeo, nec alia est ratio Ecclesiæ colligendæ & collectæ: nec sanè aliam concedamus, ex eo causa Pontificia [?] quicquam adiuuari potest. Verum est, Ecclesiam primum per fidem Catholicam collectam vocatamque: deinde eandem fidem, tanquam ignem illum de cœlo, in eadem Ecclesia integram conseruari, proponi, & prædicari.
units.tr: I reply: neither is there any other way of gathering and assembling the Church, nor should we concede any other, for the Papists' cause can gain nothing from it. It is true that the Church was first gathered and called through the Catholic faith; then that same faith, like that fire from heaven, is preserved whole in the same Church, set forth and preached.

units.la: Sed isti toto aberrant cœlo. Fingunt enim, se Ecclesiam esse. Populum autem, qui sedet in tenebris, è quibus Ecclesia Christi usque ad finem mundi perpetuo est colligenda, prorsus negligunt. Tenebras illas ex industria augent, verbi lucem sedulo abscondunt, fidem Catholicam Ecclesiæ traditam non custodiunt, sed prodigiosis hominum commentis & fabulis contaminatam proponunt, lucem illam, quæ à Deo est, quæ de cœlo venerat, penitus extinguunt, eius loco traditiones suas obtrudunt: in sua esse potestate clamitant, fidem dare, imo condere : Et quum lucem cœlestem in tenebras converterint, populumque, qui in Ecclesiam erat colligendus, a luce arcuerint, tum demum intrifice [?] sibi applaudunt ; & sicut meretrix impura matronæ speciem mentitur, ita meretricia fronte se iactant Ecclesiam esse, imo vero Ecclesiam matrem, quæ errare non possit. Ad hanc impudentiam retundendam, quædam necessario dicenda sunt, quæ nos ordine prosequemur : multa sunt, quæ somniant isti : se Ecclesiam esse, fidem ab illis sumendam. Primo de fide dicamus, quod instituimus.
units.tr: But these men are wide of the mark. For they pretend that they themselves are the Church. Meanwhile they utterly neglect the people who sit in darkness, from which the Church of Christ must be continually gathered until the end of the world. They deliberately increase that darkness, diligently hide the light of the Word, do not keep the Catholic faith delivered to the Church, but put forward a faith contaminated by monstrous human inventions and fables, utterly extinguish that light which is from God and came down from heaven, and in its place force their own traditions upon us. They cry out that it is in their power to give faith, indeed to make it. And when they have turned the heavenly light into darkness and kept the people who were to be gathered into the Church away from the light, then at last they applaud themselves; and, like an impure harlot who pretends to be a matron, they boast with a harlot's brazenness that they are the Church, indeed the mother Church, which cannot err. To beat back this impudence certain things must necessarily be said, which we shall pursue in order: there are many things these men dream, that they are the Church and that faith is to be received from them. First let us speak of faith, as we set out to do.

units.la: Docuimus, Ecclesiam per fidem Catholicam collectam fuisse atque vocatam. Natura autem fidei non mutatur, nec natura Ecclesiæ. Eodem igitur modo Ecclesia usque ad finem mundi vocanda est. Apostoli enim quum Ecclesias collegerunt, non sua commenta, aut traditiones, sed fidem veram proposuerunt ; non ex ingenio arbitrioque suo docuerunt, sed a Spiritu Dei acceperunt, quod Ecclesiis tradiderunt. Fides ergo Ecclesiæ non erat ab Apostolis, sed ex Deo, per Apostolorum ministerium Ecclesiæ tradita. Ecclesia igitur fidem Catholicam habet, tanquam regulam suam.
units.tr: We have taught that the Church was gathered and called through the Catholic faith. But the nature of faith does not change, nor does the nature of the Church. Therefore the Church must be called in the same way until the end of the world. For when the Apostles gathered Churches, they set forth not their own inventions or traditions, but the true faith; they did not teach from their own wit and judgment, but received from the Spirit of God what they handed on to the Churches. The faith of the Church was therefore not from the Apostles, but from God, delivered to the Church through the ministry of the Apostles. The Church therefore has the Catholic faith as its rule.

units.la: Sed nisi fides ipsa suam etiam regulam habeat, incerta erit, & semper in periculo, ne vel mutetur, vel penitus amittatur. Jam vero, quia fides Ecclesiæ ex Deo est, non ex hominibus, necesse est, ut regula fidei ex Deo sit.
units.tr: But unless the faith itself has its own rule, it will be uncertain and always in danger of either being changed or utterly lost. Now, since the faith of the Church is from God, not from men, it is necessary that the rule of faith also be from God.

units.la: Quomodo enim potest id, quod ex hominibus est determinare, definire, & potestatem exercere in id, quod à Deo est. Regula igitur fidei ex Deo est. Fides, inquit Apostolus, ex auditu est, auditus per verbum Dei. Verbum ergo illud Dei, ex cuius auditu fides oritur, est fidei regula. At verbum illud Dei in sacra Scriptura continetur. Ecclesiæ igitur regula est fides Catholica: fidei autem regula sacra Scriptura. Neque vero interesse arbitramur, Scripturamne dicamus regulam fidei; an Symbolum illud Apostolicum, in quo sacræ Scripturæ summam atque epitomen tradicam[?] suscepit Ecclesia. Quicunque enim Symbolum exposuerunt ex antiquis, omnes articulos ex sacra Scriptura probarunt & confirmarunt. Itaque Symbolum etiam ad Scripturas, tanquam ad regulam revocant.
units.tr: For how can that which is from men determine and define that which is from God, and exercise authority over it? The rule of faith is therefore from God. "Faith," says the Apostle, "comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of God" [Rom. 10.17]. The word of God, then, from the hearing of which faith arises, is the rule of faith. But that word of God is contained in holy Scripture. The rule of the Church is therefore the Catholic faith, and the rule of faith is holy Scripture. Nor do we think it makes any difference whether we call Scripture the rule of faith or that Apostles' Creed, in which the Church has received the sum and epitome of holy Scripture. For all who expounded the creed among the ancients proved and confirmed every article from holy Scripture. Thus they also refer the creed back to the Scriptures as to the rule.

units.la: Ex iis, quæ diximus, non erit difficile, hæc tria, Ecclesiam, fidem, Scripturas, ad sua munia revocare. Nam fides Catholica regit Ecclesiam, Scripturæ fidem. Jam si de autoritate quæritur, quis nescit maiorem esse autoritatem eius, quod regit, quam quod regitur? Quum igitur quæstionem instituunt turbatores Tridentini de autoritate Ecclesiæ, & Scripturarum; & Scripturas pendere velint ex autoritate Ecclesiæ: Ecclesia Catholica contra hunc errorem constanter semper docuit, Ecclesiam, & Ecclesiæ fidem demonstrari autoritate Scripturarum: Scripturas autem confetuari[?], & tanquam cœlestes thesauros recondi, & di,&custodiri ab Ecclesia. Autoritas igitur est Scripturarum, ministerium vero Ecclesiæ. Ecclefia igitur ex autoritate Scripturarum fidem Catholicam custodit, proponit, exponit, confirmat. Atque hoc ministerio maxime probatur ac demonstratur Ecclesia vera. Ita Ecclesia optime cognoscitur per fidei regulam ; fidei regula per Scripturas, ac proinde Ecclesia per Scripturas.
units.tr: From what we have said it will not be difficult to refer these three things, the Church, the faith and the Scriptures, to their proper offices. For the Catholic faith governs the Church, and the Scriptures govern the faith. Now if the question is about authority, who does not know that the authority of that which governs is greater than that of what is governed? Since, therefore, the Tridentine troublemakers raise the question of the authority of the Church and of the Scriptures, and wish the Scriptures to depend on the authority of the Church, the Catholic Church has always constantly taught against this error that the Church and the Church's faith are demonstrated by the authority of the Scriptures, while the Scriptures are preserved and, like heavenly treasures, stored up and guarded by the Church. The authority, then, belongs to the Scriptures, and the ministry to the Church. The Church therefore keeps, sets forth, expounds and confirms the Catholic faith by the authority of the Scriptures. And it is by this ministry above all that the true Church is proved and demonstrated. Thus the Church is best known through the rule of faith; the rule of faith through the Scriptures, and therefore the Church through the Scriptures.

units.la: Sed priusquam Ecclesiæ consensum de hac re proferamus; duo sunt inprimis obseruanda. Primum, in quo Aduersariorum consensum habemus: Ecclesiam optime cognosci per regulam fidei: in hac re mutuus est consensus. Secundum, in quo est controuersia: non enim conuenit inter nos, quænam sit illa regula fidei. Nam Pontificii nuper circa tempora Concilii Tridentini commentum hoc excogitarunt, quod antiquos omnes laruit, regulam fidei totalem esse Scripturas & traditiones non scriptas: ita vt sacræ Scripturæ sint vna pars huius regulæ, altera pars traditiones. Verum Tridentini Patres sero sapiunt. Nam antiqua Ecclesiæ sapientia commentum hoc respuit. Probant Patres Ecclesiæ magno consen-su, regulam fidei prorsus esse immutabilem, quod supra demonstrauimus. Regula igitur illa, quæ per Tridentinos mutata est, non est fidei regula: quia hæc vnica, eadem, immutata per omnes Ecclesiæ successiones decurrit. Et proinde vnitas etiam Ecclesiæ pendet ex hac vnitate regulæ fidei. Diuersa & mutata fides, diuersa & mutata fidei regula, Ecclesiam probant diuersam & mutatam. Vna, & non mutata est Christi Ecclesia: diuersa & mutata Antichristi. Antiqui autem Scriptores uniuersi, usque ad tempora Concilii Tridentini, regulam fidei docent esse Scripturas canonicas, quum de regula completa disputant, vel Symbolum Apostolicum, quum de regula summaria loquuntur. Praeter hanc fidei regulam vel summatim in Symbolo, vel fusius in Scripturis canonicis positam, nullam prorsus agnoscunt. Quoties igitur Ecclesiam quaerunt, per hanc regulam quaerunt, hoc est, per Scripturas canonicas. Qua in re contra Tridentinos ad omnes antiquos Scriptores Ecclesiae, atq; adeo ad Ecclesiae uniuersae consensum provocamus.
units.tr: But before we bring forward the consent of the Church on this matter, two things must first be observed. The first is that on which we have agreement with our opponents: the Church is best known through the rule of faith; in this matter the consensus is mutual. The second is where the controversy lies: for we do not agree about what that rule of faith is. For the Papists, only recently, around the time of the Council of Trent, devised this fiction, which escaped all the ancients, that the whole rule of faith consists of Scriptures and unwritten traditions, so that the holy Scriptures are one part of this rule and the traditions the other. But the Tridentine Fathers are wise too late. For the wisdom of the ancient Church rejects this fiction. The Fathers of the Church with great unanimity prove that the rule of faith is wholly unchangeable, as we demonstrated above. That rule, therefore, which has been altered by the Tridentines, is not the rule of faith, because the true rule is one, the same, and unchanged, and runs through all the successions of the Church. And so the unity of the Church also depends on this unity of the rule of faith. A different and changed faith proves a different and changed rule of faith, and that proves the Church different and changed. The Church of Christ is one and unchanged; that of Antichrist is diverse and changed. But all the ancient writers, up to the time of the Council of Trent, teach that the rule of faith is the canonical Scriptures, when they discuss the complete rule, or the Apostles' Creed, when they speak of the summary rule. Besides this rule of faith, set down either briefly in the Creed or more fully in the canonical Scriptures, they acknowledge no other at all. Whenever, therefore, they seek the Church, they seek it through this rule, that is, through the canonical Scriptures. In this matter we appeal against the Tridentines to all the ancient writers of the Church, and so to the consensus of the whole Church.

units.la: CAPUT X. Testimonia Patrum, demonstrantia Ec-clesiam per regulam fidei, siue per Scripturas ca-nonicas.
units.tr: CHAPTER X. Testimonies of the Fathers showing that the Church is known by the rule of faith, or by the canonical Scriptures.

units.la: CLemens Alexandrinus sic docet: {a}Ec-clesiam antiquam & Catholicam esse dicimus, in unitatem unius fidei, quae est ex propriis testamen-tis, vel potius ex testamento, quod est unum diuersis temporibus. Haec ille. Cuius accurata & distincta loquendi formula obseruanda est. Ecclesiam Catholicam, & antiquam, quaeritin unitate fidei; fidem autem in duobus testamentis. Ita
units.tr: Clement of Alexandria teaches as follows: We say that the ancient and Catholic Church is in the unity of one faith, which comes from the proper testaments, or rather from the one testament that is one across different times. So he. His exact and distinct manner of speaking must be observed. He seeks the ancient and Catholic Church in the unity of faith, and he seeks the faith in the two Testaments. So too,

units.la: {a} lib.7.Stro-mat. Ecclesiæ regulam docet esse fidem, fidei regulam duo Testamenta.
units.tr: in book 7 of the Stromata, he teaches that the rule of the Church is the faith, and the rule of the faith is the two Testaments.

units.la: Origenes : {a} Qui iniquitatem in excelso loquuntur, & extendunt in cœlum os suum, sicut hæretici faciunt, incircumcisi. & immundis labijs dicendi sunt. Circumcisus labijs & mundus est, qui semper verbum Dei loquitur, & sanam doctrinam Evangelicus & Apostolicus munitam regulam profert. Hæcil-le. Qui verbum Dei, & sana doctrinam Euangelicis & Apostolicis regulis muniendam docuit, certe sicut Ecclesiam per doctrinam, ita doctrinam per Scripturas probandam esse probabat: & traditiones non scriptas plane reiicit; quia quæ scripta non sunt, non muniuntur regulis Euangelicis & Apostolicis. Idemque sic habet: {b} Ecclesia dos suis Legis & Prophetarum volumina. Hæcille. Dotem Ecclesiæ Scripturas esse docet. Si Ecclesia Scripturas habet pro dote, unde, aut quo titulo contraxit traditiones non scriptas?
units.tr: Origen: Those who speak iniquity on high, and stretch their mouth to heaven, as heretics do, are uncircumcised and must be called unclean of lips. He is circumcised in lips and clean who always speaks the word of God and sets forth sound doctrine, fortified by the Gospel and Apostolic rule. So he. He who taught that the word of God and sound doctrine must be fortified by Gospel and Apostolic rules plainly showed that the Church must be proved by doctrine, and doctrine by the Scriptures; and he flatly rejects unwritten traditions, because what is not written is not fortified by Gospel and Apostolic rules. He likewise says: The Church has the volumes of the Law and the Prophets as her dowry. So he. He teaches that the Scriptures are the dowry of the Church. If the Church has the Scriptures as her dowry, from what source, or by what title, has she acquired unwritten traditions?

units.la: Athanasius: {c} Orthodoxa Ecclesia recte legens, & exacte sacras Scripturas examinans, seipsam ædificat super petram. Quibus verbis describit Ecclesiæ ministerium. In hoc ministerio Scripturam sibi regulam proponit, quia ædificatio Ecclesiæ est per Scripturas, non autem per traditiones non scriptas.
units.tr: Athanasius: The orthodox Church, reading rightly and examining the holy Scriptures exactly, builds herself upon the rock. In these words he describes the ministry of the Church. In this ministry she sets Scripture before herself as her rule, because the building up of the Church is through the Scriptures, not through unwritten traditions.

units.la: Chrysostomus in illa verba: Ecclesia domus Dei viventis, columna & firmamentum veritatis. {d} Ecclesia est, inquit, quæ fidem continet, & prædicationem: quippe veritas Ecclesia & columna est, & firmamentum. Hæc ille. Docet igitur, Ecclesiam optime cognosci ex ministerio suo in confer- tuanda & prædicanda veritatis doctrina.
units.tr: Chrysostom, on the words: The Church is the house of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. The Church, he says, is what holds the faith and the preaching: for the truth is the Church, and its pillar and ground. So he. He therefore teaches that the Church is best known from her ministry in preserving and preaching the doctrine of the truth.

units.la: [?]Iisdem optime conspirant ea, quæ habet autor operis imperfecti in Matth. {a}Qui vult, inquit, cognoscere, quæ sit vera Ecclesia Christi, unde cognoscat, nisi tantummodo per Scripturas? Quo loco vberrimus est in eandem sententiam: Docet enim, Ecclesiam Christi quondam variis modis distingui potuisse à gentilitate, sed regnante Antichristo, nullam aliam viam reliquam futuram cognoscendi Ecclesiam veram, inquit, nisi tantummodo per Scripturas: quia omnia ea, quæ sunt proprie Christi in veritate, habet Antichristus in schismate. Similiter Ecclesias[?], similiter ipsas Scripturas diuinas, similiter Episcopos, cæterosque ordines clericorum, & Sacramenta. Ergo volens cognoscere, quæ sit vera Ecclesia Christi, unde cognoscat in tanta confusione similitudinis, nisi tantummodo per Scripturas? Hæc ille.
units.tr: The works of the author of the Opus Imperfectum on Matthew agree very well with these same things: He who wishes to know what the true Church of Christ is, he says, from what could he know it, except only through the Scriptures? In this passage he is abundantly of the same opinion.
