units.la: potuit sine Romano Pontifice, quæ autoritatem in Romanum Pontificem exercere solebat, quæ Romanos Pontifices examinare, iudicare, coërcere, deponere potuit? Quid possunt respondere, quam vel hanc Ecclesiam omnino periisse, nec esse iam in rerum natura; vel apud eos esse, qui reformatas Ecclesias obtinent? Perire Ecclesia Christi non potest; sequitur ergo, ut apud nos esse, quamquam inviti, fateantur. Nam quæ hodie apud Pontificios Ecclesia esse videtur, quid aliud est, quam Romana illa Curia, ex Papa & adulatoribus conflata, à qua maiores nostri semper appellare ad Romanam Catholicam Ecclesiam consueverunt. In his rebus confirmandis eorum testimonia contra hodiernos Pontificios proferimus, qui apud ipsos omni exceptione maiores esse debent.
units.tr: Which Church, which could exercise authority over the Roman Pontiff, and examine, judge, restrain and depose the Roman Pontiffs, can they point to that could exist without the Roman Pontiff? What can they answer, except either that this Church has altogether perished and no longer exists in the nature of things, or that it is among those who hold the reformed Churches? The Church of Christ cannot perish; it follows, therefore, that they must admit, however unwillingly, that it is among us. For what is today seen as the Church among the Papists is nothing other than that Roman Curia, compounded of the Pope and his flatterers, to which our forefathers were always accustomed to appeal from the Roman Catholic Church. In confirming these matters we bring forward their testimonies against the present-day Papists, which ought to be beyond all exception among them as their own forefathers.

units.la: Tria Concilia, Pisanum, Constantiense, Basiliense, ostendunt nobis consensum iudiciumque Ecclesiæ Romanæ, & doctissimorum virorum, qui in illis Ecclesiæ seculis vixerunt. Pisanum Concilium authoritate sua deposuit Gregorium XII. & Benedictum XIII. Constantiensis Synodus authoritatem Concilii generalis super Papam sic declarat: a Sancta hæc Synodus declarat, quod ipsa in Spiritu sancto legitime congregata, Concilium generale faciens, & Ecclesiam Catholicam repræsentans, potestatem à Christo immediate habet, cuiuscunque status & conditionis, etiamsi Papalis existat, obedire tenetur in his [?], quæ perpertinent ad fidem, & reformationem in Capite, & membris. Quibus verbis recentia ista Iesuitarum figmenta reiiciuntur.
units.tr: Three Councils, Pisa, Constance and Basel, show us the consensus and judgement of the Roman Church and of the most learned men who lived in those ages of the Church. The Council of Pisa by its own authority deposed Gregory XII and Benedict XIII. The Synod of Constance declares the authority of a general council over the Pope in these words: This holy Synod declares that it, lawfully assembled in the Holy Spirit, forming a general council and representing the Catholic Church, has its power immediately from Christ, and that everyone, of whatever state or condition, even if he be of papal dignity, is bound to obey it in those matters which pertain to faith, and to the reformation of the Head and the members. By these words those recent figments of the Jesuits are rejected.

units.la: Docent Iesuitæ, Papam esse super Concilium, & Ecclesiam: Constantienses affirmant, Ecclesiam esse super Papam. Clamant isti, Episcopos potestatem accipere à Papa: Constantienses vero, Episcopos immediate à CHRISTO potestatem habere, statuunt. Quibus etiam consentanea in Concilio Basiliensi habentur, sic enim docent: {a}Veri-tas de potestate Concilii generalis universam Ecclesiam repræsentantis, super Papam, & quemlibet alterum, declarata per Constantiense, & hoc Basiliense, generalia Concilia, est veritas fidei Catholicæ. Idemque sæpius repetunt in eadem sessione. Sic etiam docent iidem Patres: {b}Certum est, Papam errare posse: experientia etiam demonstrat, quia sæpe experti sumus, & legimus, Papam errasse. {c}Universalis Ecclesia sæpe obedientiam Romanis Pontificibus subtraxit, Marcellino, Anastasio, Liberio, Iohanni XII. Benedicto IX. Benedicto XIII. Iohanni XXIII.
units.tr: The Jesuits teach that the Pope is above the Council and the Church; the Constantinians affirm that the Church is above the Pope. Those men cry out that bishops receive their power from the Pope; but the Constantinians lay down that bishops have their power immediately from CHRIST. Things consistent with this are also found in the Council of Basel, for they teach thus: The truth concerning the power of a general council, representing the universal Church, over the Pope and any other person, declared by the general councils of Constance and of this Basel, is a truth of the Catholic faith. And the same men repeat this often in the same session. The same Fathers also teach: It is certain that the Pope can err; experience too shows it, since we have often found and read that the Pope has erred. The universal Church has often withdrawn obedience from Roman Pontiffs: Marcellinus, Anastasius, Liberius, John XII, Benedict IX, Benedict XIII, John XXIII.

units.la: Exclamet hic Bellarminus, quantum volet, exclament Iesuitæ omnes, hæc Concilia partim esse approbata, partim reprobata: hæc autem, quæ de potestate Ecclesiæ super Papam statuuntur, reprobata esse: num possunt tam frigidis commentis persuadere hominibus cordatis, Papam cum sua Curia habere authoritatem reprobandi ea, quæ in Conciliis statuuntur? Facetos homihomines, qui pro libidine sua, quæ placent, accipiunt, quæ non placent, expungunt. Ut-cunque se in omnes colores immutent, nunquam eripient nobis veritatem.
units.tr: Let Bellarmine cry out as much as he likes, let all the Jesuits exclaim that these Councils are partly approved and partly rejected, and that those things which are laid down about the power of the Church over the Pope are rejected: can they persuade sensible men with such cold inventions that the Pope with his Curia has authority to reject what is decreed in the Councils? Witty fellows, who accept what pleases them at will and strike out what does not! However they change themselves into every colour, they will never snatch the truth from us.

units.la: Nos ex Romanæ Ecclesiæ Conciliis testimonia producimus. Negant Iesuitæ, appro-bata esse hæc Concilia in iis, quæ contra auto-ritatem Papæ statuuntur; quanquam impu-denter negent; tamen esto. At quod nos affir-mamus, negare non possunt. Producimus doc-tissimorum eius seculi hominum iudicia in illis Conciliis. Non Canones Conciliorum urgemus, sed eorum iudicia, sententiasque exquirimus, qui tunc in Romana Ecclesia celeberrimi habebantur. Ut inde, quæ fuerat maiorum nostrorum religio, quis sensus, quodnam iudicium, intelligamus; imo ut quæ tunc temporis fuerit Ecclesiæ Romanæ sententia, sensusque constare possit. Qui enim in illis Conciliis congregati erant, Ecclesiam Romanam repræsentare putabantur: sicut Romana Ecclesia intelligitur, Ecclesiarum in orbis Christiani partibus collectio. Si enim istos auferas, ubi tandem erat Romana Ecclesia? Ex horum igitur sententiis, hoc est, ex Ecclesiæ Romanæ sententia, qualis autorum nostrorum memoria Romanæ Ecclesiæ religio fuerit, constat. Nondum enim recepti in Ecclesia fuerunt errores isti, quos nunc Iesuitæ maximis clamoribus ingeminant. Atq; hæc nobis huius mali originem aperient, quod est instituti nostri investigare. C tem lent bus sole vel per est; clef ta, mn sub stu Ch Ch re. ma po Ec Pa Ci Ca tu ni rusti id id tu C su e
units.tr: We bring forward testimonies from the Councils of the Roman Church. The Jesuits deny that these Councils are approved in those matters which are decreed against the authority of the Pope; yet, though they deny it shamelessly, let it be so. But what we affirm, they cannot deny. We produce the judgements of the most learned men of that age in those Councils. We do not press the canons of the Councils, but seek out their judgements and opinions, of those who were then most celebrated in the Roman Church. From this we may understand what the religion of our forefathers was, and what their sense and judgement was; indeed, what the opinion and sense of the Roman Church was at that time may be established. For those who were gathered in those Councils were thought to represent the Roman Church, just as the Roman Church is understood to be the collection of Churches in the parts of the Christian world. For if you remove these, where at last was the Roman Church? From their opinions, therefore, that is, from the opinion of the Roman Church, it is established what the religion of the Roman Church was in the memory of our authors. For those errors which the Jesuits now repeat with the loudest clamours had not yet been received in the Church. And these things will open to us the origin of this evil, which is the purpose of our undertaking to investigate.

units.la: Cognoscant igitur Ecclesiæ suæ antiquiratem, qui de Ecclesia tanto hiatu iactare solent. Ecclesia ista Iesuitica mutata est in omnibus iis, quibus Ecclesia Christi demonstrari solebat. Ecclesia enim demonstrari solebat, vel per Caput suum, vel per membra sua, vel per regulam suam. Caput Ecclesiæ Christus est; membra Ecclesiæ, Sancti sunt: regula Ecclesiæ, est regula fidei è sacris Scripturis petita, in sacris Scripturis comprehensa. Hæc omnia mutantur à Iesuitis. Pro Christo Capite substituunt Romanum Pontificem; ita Christum excludunt. At dicent Iesuitæ, non se Christum excludere: sed quum Vicarium Christi agnoscant, Christum etiam agnoscere. Respondeo: Hæc verba sunt inania, & meræ nugæ, quibus simplicibus se illudere posse sperant. At num & Christum, & Christi Ecclesiam suis fallaciis se decepturos sperant? Papa, inquiunt, est vice Christi in Ecclesia. At Christus est Caput sanctorum, non autem Caput eorum, in quibus nulla est interna virtus. Papa vero Caput est impiorum, in quibus nulla est interna virtus, ex doctrina Iesuitarum. Quomodo ergo potest Papa esse Christi Vicarius? Regit Christus Ecclesiam suam, id est, sanctos: At regit Papa Ecclesiam aliam, id est, profanos, in quibus fides non requiritur. Non potest igitur Papa esse Vicarius Christi in Ecclesia; quia non regit eandem sub Christo Ecclesiam. Christus igitur plane excluditur ab Ecclesia Pontificia, & pro Christo Romanum Pontificem substituunt Iesuitæ: pro sanctis Ecclesiæ membris obtrudunt improbos, & reprobos: pro regula fidei in Scripturis, supponunt Romani Pontificis placita in traditionibus.
units.tr: Let those who are often wont to boast of the antiquity of their Church, with such great gaping, now recognise it. That Jesuit Church has changed in all those respects by which the Church of Christ used to be shown. For the Church used to be shown either by its Head, or by its members, or by its rule. The Head of the Church is Christ; the members of the Church are the saints; the rule of the Church is the rule of faith, drawn from the holy Scriptures and contained in them. All these things are changed by the Jesuits. In place of Christ as Head they substitute the Roman Pontiff; thus they exclude Christ. But the Jesuits will say that they do not exclude Christ, but, since they acknowledge the Vicar of Christ, they also acknowledge Christ. I answer: these words are empty and mere trifles, with which they hope to deceive simple folk. But do they hope to deceive Christ and the Church of Christ with their tricks too? The Pope, they say, is in the Church in the place of Christ. But Christ is the Head of the saints, not of those in whom there is no inward virtue. Yet the Pope is the head of the impious, in whom there is no inward virtue, according to the teaching of the Jesuits. How then can the Pope be the Vicar of Christ? Christ rules his Church, that is, the saints; but the Pope rules another Church, that is, the profane, in whom faith is not required. The Pope therefore cannot be the Vicar of Christ in the Church, because he does not rule the same Church under Christ. Christ, then, is plainly excluded from the Pontifical Church, and the Jesuits substitute the Roman Pontiff for Christ; in place of the saints as members of the Church they thrust in the wicked and the reprobate; in place of the rule of faith in the Scriptures, they put up the decrees of the Roman Pontiff in traditions.

units.la: Atque hæc est Ecclesia illa nuper exorta, quam pro Ecclesia Christi proponunt Iesuitæ. Ecclesia scilicet, in cuius regimine [?]sedet Romanus Pontifex, qui sit Caput Ecclesiæ, supra[?] Ecclesiam, qui solus errare non possit, sine quo Ecclesia potest errare, quique à nemine iudicari debeat: cuius membra sint homines sine vlla interna virtute, externa tantum professione coniuncti, & Sacramentorum communione, quæ sensu ipso percipitur: cuius regula sint traditiones non scriptæ, vel os Rom. Pontificis. Hanc Ecclesiam cum hoc Rege, cum his membris, cum hac regula, vnicam, veram, Apostolicam, Romanam scilicet, & sanctam, etiam agnoscunt Iesuitæ. Nos vero diserte pronuntiamus, hanc Ecclesiam, cum hoc Rege, cum his membris, cum hac regula, post Constantiensis, & Basiliensis Conciliorum tempora inualuisse. Num quid causæ erit, quod de antiquitate glorientur, qui Ecclesiæ suæ incunabula prima, non ante Concilium Tridentinum, hoc est, vix ante quadraginta annos reperiunt?
units.tr: And this is that Church, lately sprung up, which the Jesuits put forward as the Church of Christ: a Church in whose government [?] sits the Roman Pontiff, who is the Head of the Church, above the Church, who alone cannot err, without whom the Church can err, and who ought to be judged by no one; whose members are men without any inward virtue, joined only by outward profession and communion in the sacraments, which is perceived by the senses alone; whose rule is unwritten traditions or the mouth of the Roman Pontiff. This Church, with this King, with these members, with this rule, the Jesuits also acknowledge as one, true, Apostolic, namely Roman, and holy. But we plainly declare that this Church, with this King, with these members, with this rule, prevailed only after the times of the Councils of Constance and Basel. Is there any reason why they should boast of antiquity, who find the first cradle of their Church not before the Council of Trent, that is, scarcely forty years ago?

units.la: Ante Aquinatem de Ecclesia, de Capite, de membris, de regula, integra sunt omnia. Qui de Ecclesia disputarunt, Catholicam describunt, esse cœtum sanctorum, esse corpus Christi, in quo impiis & profanis hominibus non est locus. Si de Romana Ecclesia mentio-nem faciant, honorifice [illegible, ~6 letters] Ecclesiæ Christi membrum, & quidem illustre admittunt: at-que inter visibiles, & particulares Ecclesias, Romanam fuisse, in occiduis orbis partibus, veluti Principem. Neq; aliter nos de Romana Ecclesia loquimur, aut sentimus, quamdiu veritas apud eam valuit. Postea lubrepsit error: & privatæ fraterculorum opiniones contra antiquam Ecclesiæ doctrinam invectæ sunt: tandem omnis Ecclesiæ potestas in Romano Pontifice statuitur. Atque hæc est Ecclesia illa, & Ecclesiæ potestas, pro qua sola Iesuitæ pugnant. Nos, quia hanc Ecclesiam neque in Scripturis, neque in Patrum monumentis, ne quidem in veterum Pontificiorum scriptis invenire possumus; quia contra hanc Ecclesiam, Scripturarum, Patrum, atq; Conciliorum recentium testimonia gravissima adducimus, quibus lucu-lentissime constare possit, errores fraterculorum, iam tum in Ecclesiam Romanam non fuisse receptos: merito concludimus, hanc Ecclesiam, quam hodie solam probant Pontificii, non esse Catholicam, sed à Catholica mutaram [?], nec aute Concilii Tridentini tempora extructam fuisse.
units.tr: Before Aquinas, everything concerning the Church, the Head, the members and the rule was intact. Those who disputed about the Church describe the Catholic Church as the assembly of the saints, the body of Christ, in which there is no place for impious and profane men. If they make mention of the Roman Church, they honourably admit it as a member of the Church of Christ, and indeed an illustrious one, and among the visible and particular Churches they regard it as having been the leading one in the western parts of the world. Nor do we speak or think otherwise of the Roman Church, so long as the truth prevailed in it. Afterwards error crept in, and the private opinions of little friars were brought in against the ancient doctrine of the Church; at last all power of the Church was placed in the Roman Pontiff. And this is that Church, and that power of the Church, for which the Jesuits alone fight. We, because we cannot find this Church either in the Scriptures, or in the monuments of the Fathers, nor even in the writings of the older Papists; because against this Church we bring the most weighty testimonies of the Scriptures, the Fathers and the recent Councils, by which it can be most clearly established that the errors of the little friars had not yet been received into the Roman Church, we rightly conclude that this Church, which the Papists alone now approve, is not Catholic, but has been changed from the Catholic, and was built not before the times of the Council of Trent.

units.la: Summa controversiæ huius est in defini-tione Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: The whole of this controversy lies in the definition of the Church.

units.la: Dicimus, aliam esse huius verbi mentem, alium hodie sensum à Iesuitis inueinuectum, quam fuerat olim. Ecclesia perpetuo vna est; fundamentum habet doctrinam Apostolorum, & Prophetarum, cuius angularis lapis est Iesus Christus. Hodierna vero Pontificia Ecclesia nuper è fraterculorum lacunis exorta, fundamentum habet, Tridentina decreta, cuius angularis lapis est Romanus Pontifex. Ecclesia Christi vnica est, semperque eadem. Sed Pontificia alia est, atque alia. Aliud fundamentum, aliud Caput, alius angularis lapis, alia membra, alia regula fidei probant mutatam Ecclesiam. Quia ergo essentialia mutantur in hac, quam Iesuitae nobis proponunt, Ecclesia, dicimus ex Ecclesia Christi, factam esse Ecclesiam Antichristi.
units.tr: We say that the Jesuits have brought in a different meaning for this word, and a different sense from the one it had long ago. The Church is always one; it has as its foundation the doctrine of the Apostles and Prophets, of which Jesus Christ is the chief cornerstone. But the present Papist Church, lately sprung from the pits of the little friars, has as its foundation the decrees of Trent, and as its chief cornerstone the Roman Pontiff. The Church of Christ is one and always the same. But the Papist Church is another thing altogether. A different foundation, a different head, a different cornerstone, different members and a different rule of faith prove that the Church has been changed. Because the essentials are changed in this Church, which the Jesuits set before us, we say that the Church of Christ has become the Church of Antichrist.

units.la: Postremo ipsam Ecclesiae Romanae vocem gemitumque querimoniae plenam audiamus. Nam ante reformationem à Luthero partim inchoatam, Ecclesia sub Antichristi tyrannide oppressa ingemuit. Dum enim superbae tyrannidi reluctatur, dum dominatum improbum exhorret, dum liberationem exspectat, captiuitatis suae conscium emisit gemitum. Non hic Waldensium, aut Wiclefistarum testimonia, sed ipsius Romanae Ecclesiae gemitum, sub Antichristi tyrannide captae, atque oppressae, subiungam. Nam qui in Basiliensi Concilio convenerunt, eos ex Romana Ecclesia fuisse, fatentur Adversarii: horum querimoniam gravissimam, quanquam longiorem, subnectam tamen; ut Babylonica ista ca-ptiuitas, ipsorum captiuorum testimonio, luculenerpeinam gulavero m laentiā omaemque alius fidei o efobis esia cem ous. timide tyroat, m. teniue nsi ecieoauriculentius constare possit. Sic ergo miserabi-lem ruentis Ecclesiæ statum deplorant illi:
units.tr: Last of all, let us hear the voice of the Roman Church itself, full of groaning and complaint. For before the reformation partly begun by Luther, the Church, oppressed under the tyranny of Antichrist, groaned. For while it struggled against proud tyranny, while it abhorred wicked domination and waited for deliverance, it uttered a groan, conscious of its captivity. I will add here not the testimonies of the Waldenses or the Wycliffites, but the groan of the Roman Church itself, captured and oppressed under the tyranny of Antichrist. For our opponents admit that those who gathered at the Council of Basel came from the Roman Church. I will append their very grave complaint, though it is rather long, so that this Babylonian captivity may be shown more clearly from the testimony of the captives themselves. Thus those men lament the wretched state of the collapsing Church:

units.la: Animaduertite inprimis, o Christicolæ, & ante oculos vestros ponite miserandum & flebilem sta-tum religionis Christianæ, si eo redacta fuerit, vt quisq; in summâ Pontificiâ positus, iam assecutus sit, quod nullam correctionem à Concilijs generali-bus habeat pertimescere, quantumcunq; Ecclesiam scandalizet, & eius statum perturbet, ac decolorét: ita vt si omnes dignitates Ecclesiasticas, & beneficia vendéret, si Prælatos quosq; inuitos transferret, & expelleret iniuste pro libito voluntatis, etiam notorie, ac iniuste Reges ac Principes deiiceret, moribus per-niciosis animas hominum passim perimere laboraret, crudelitates perpetraret horrendas, Legem Dei con-funderet, quaq; salubria instituta everteret, tempo-ralia Ecclesia Romana, & caeterarum particularium Ecclesiarum dissiparet, atq; alienaret; aliaq; immu-[?] mera flagitia, scelera, & crimina notoria perpetra-ret, ac se incorrigibilem redderet: Omnes Ecclesiae in vnam congregatâ, nullatenus eum à talibus coercere possit: quinimo liberum sit, quamlibet Synodum, eum reprimere volentem, illico transferre, vel dissoluere persistentes in Synodo contra volantem eius perse-qui, excommunicare, priuare, inhabilitare, contume-liâ & iniuriis afficere, inuasiones corporales ad-uersus eos excitare; deinde quicquid Synodus sta-tueret, præciperet, distaret, ordinaret, penitus con-temnere, abiicere, reprobare. Conspicite pro Dei re-uerentia, qualis ex hac re daretur iniuria in suam humani generis, ad subuertendam religionem Chri-stianam, dum seducendo vnum hominem, posset „Christianitatem in maximam desolationem deiicere, mores peruertere, canones, & regulas quasque dissipare Ecclesiasticas, Regna, & prouincias conturbare, ac bonis spiritualibus, & temporalibus spoliare, vitiorumque immanitatem introducere. Aperite oculos, & videte, qualis ex hoc duratur ingressus Antichristo. Sed & considerate quomodo ea res fidem catholicam confunderet, atque violaret, quae est primum fundamentum Ecclesiastici aedificii, quo euerso omnia corruunt. Haec illi, & plura etiam in hanc sententiam.
units.tr: Take note first of all, O Christians, and set before your eyes the miserable and lamentable state of the Christian religion, if it has been brought to such a point that anyone placed in the highest Papal office has achieved this, that he has no need to fear any correction from general councils, however much he scandalizes the Church and disturbs and disfigures its state; so that if he were to sell all ecclesiastical dignities and benefits, if he were to transfer and expel unjustly at his own pleasure any prelates whatever against their will, even depose kings and princes, notoriously and unjustly, if he were to labour to destroy the souls of men everywhere by pernicious morals, if he were to commit horrible cruelties, confound the law of God, overthrow wholesome institutions, squander and alienate the temporal goods of the Roman Church and of other particular Churches, and commit and persist in countless other shameful, wicked and notorious crimes, and render himself incorrigible: even if all the Churches were gathered into one, they could not in any way restrain him from such things; indeed, it would be lawful for him to transfer or dissolve any council that wished to check him, and to pursue with persecution those who persisted in the council against his will, to excommunicate, deprive, disqualify, afflict them with contumely and injuries, and stir up bodily assaults against them; and then to despise, cast off and reject utterly whatever the council decided, commanded, distributed or ordained. Look, for the reverence of God, what injury would be done by this to the human race, and to the overthrow of the Christian religion, when by seducing one man he could cast Christendom into the greatest desolation, pervert morals, scatter canons and all ecclesiastical rules, disturb kingdoms and provinces, despoil them of spiritual and temporal goods, and introduce the monstrous extent of vices. Open your eyes and see how by this an entrance is opened to Antichrist. But consider also how this matter would confound and violate the Catholic faith, which is the first foundation of the ecclesiastical building, and when it is overthrown all things fall. „These are their words, and more to the same effect.

units.la: Iam mihi [?]epora suppurate, & ab hac querimonia intra octoginta annos, Mart. Luther-us declaratus est haereticus, quum in doctrina nihil iam tentasset, tantummodo Papae tyrannidem & fraterculorum auaritiam ambitionemque vel pari libertate, vel non maiore acerbitate taxasset.
units.tr: Now, not more than eighty years ago, Martin Luther was declared a heretic, although he had attempted nothing against doctrine, but had only censured the tyranny of the Pope and the greed and ambition of the little friars, with no less freedom or no greater bitterness than they themselves had used.

units.la: Ex Basiliensium querela obseruamus 1. Ecclesiam sub Rom. Pontificis tyrânide oppressam graviter ingemuisse, & liberationem omnibus votis expetiisse. 2. Patres in hoc concilio numerasse Romanam inter particulares Ecclesias, atque eo nomine a catholica separasse Romanam, neque enim Romana vnquam catholica dicta est, nisi quatenus cum catholica consentiret, qua ratione quaevis particularis Ecclesia Catholica dici poterit. 3. Ecclesiam illam in Basiliensi Concilio collegam, fidem catholicam posuisse fundamentum Ecclesiae. 4. Ecclesiae illius iudicio fidem catholicam violatam, & subuersam iri, si tati talis [?] Princ[?] fiam, [?] cilio[?] subiect[?] tiae in[?] dei cu[?] mum [?] refact[?]
units.tr: From the complaint of the Basilians we observe: (1) that the Church, oppressed under the tyranny of the Roman Pontiff, groaned bitterly and sought deliverance with all its prayers; (2) that the Fathers at this council counted the Roman Church among the particular Churches, and on that ground separated Rome from the Catholic Church, for Rome was never called catholic except insofar as it agreed with the catholic Church, and on that reasoning any particular Church could be called catholic; (3) that the Church gathered at the Council of Basel placed the Catholic faith as the foundation of the Church; (4) that, in the judgment of that Church, the Catholic faith would be violated and overthrown if such ... [the text here is too corrupt to restore].

units.la: Qu[illegible, ~6 letters] Ponti[?] nose[?] rum [?] ficia [?] ea, n[?] temp[?] enim [?] bia, & per[?] micia [?] mult[?] coep[?] Eccl[?] firm[?] nich[?] eam[?] regn[?] form[?] dux[?] [illegible, ~4 letters] case[?] qua[?] si talis dominatus Papæ detur, vt Reges, ac Principes iniuste deiiciat, vt sit super Eccle-siam, vt non possit errare, vt Ecclesiæ,& Con-cilio generali Ecclesiam repræsentanti, non subiiciatur: si noue istæ & peregrinæ senten-tiæ in Ecclesiam recipiantur, tum demum fi-dei catholicæ ruinam denunciant, tum de-mum Antichristo ingressum in Ecclesiam pa-refactum[?] testantur.
units.tr: [The first part of this unit is illegible.] ... for at that time ... pride and ... Pope ... if such dominion of the Pope were granted that he might depose kings and princes unjustly, that he might be above the Church, that he could not err, and that he would not be subject to a general council representing the Church: if these new and foreign opinions were received into the Church, then indeed they would announce the ruin of the Catholic faith, then indeed they would testify that an entrance had been prepared for Antichrist into the Church.

units.la: Quum igitur ex eo tempore in Ecclesiam Pontificiam inuaserint ista noua dogmata, nos ex Basiliensium, id est, ex auctorum nostro-rum sententia concludimus, fidem ex Pontificia Ecclesia pulsam, Antichristum vero in ea, non tam primum ingressum, sed ex eo tempore multo magis manifestatum. Ex eo enim tempore regnum Antichristi in superbia, blasphemiis æquinoctionis mendaciis, & periuriis, clandestinis regum ruinis, ho-micidiis, veneficiis, latrociniis[?] adulteriis multo apertius, atque impudentius grassari cœpit: adeo, vt Basilienses illi si hodiernum Ecclesiæ statum viderent, non dubitarent affirmare, fidem catholicam ex Ecclesia Pon-tificia penitus profligatam, Antichristum in eam ingressum, & receptum, iam sublimem regnare: ac proinde recte, atque ex officio re-formatus Ecclesias ex Antichristi iugo se sub-duxisse.
units.tr: Since these new dogmas have invaded the Papist Church from that time, we conclude from the opinion of the Basilians, that is, of our authors, that the faith has been driven out of the Papist Church, and that Antichrist has not so much first entered it as, from that time on, been revealed far more clearly. For from that time the kingdom of Antichrist began to rage far more openly and shamelessly in pride, blasphemies, lying and perjury, in secret murders of kings, in homicides, poisonings, robberies and adulteries: so much so that those Basilians, if they saw the present state of the Church, would not hesitate to affirm that the Catholic faith has been utterly banished from the Papist Church, that Antichrist has entered and been received into it, and now reigns on high; and therefore that the reformed Churches have rightly and by their duty withdrawn themselves from the yoke of Antichrist.

units.la: Quod si obiiciant Pontificii, non Basilienses istos fuisse Ecclesiam, sed partem illam, quæcum Eugenio Papa Florentiæ secesserant
units.tr: But if the Papists object that those Basilians were not the Church, but only that part which had withdrawn with Pope Eugenius to Florence,

units.la: Respondeo: Hoc illud est, quod iam docul-mus, aliam scilicet esse Romanam Ecclesiam, aliam Romanam Curiam. Romana Ecclesia saepius sese Papae Curiaeque Romanae oppo-suit. Et quanquam Romana ista Curia cum Papa tandem victrix, conculcata Ecclesia, e-vasisse videatur: tamen originem suam co-gnoscant, genus hoc hominum humile atque ignobile ex antiquis fraterculis, recentibusque Iesuitis, qui vocationem nullam legitimam ostendere possunt in Ecclesia Christi, aliis denique adulatoribus conflatum, non ita pridem orbi innotuit, ab Ecclesia semper reiectum fuit, damnatumque ab iis, qui in Romana Ec-clesia, doctrinae, pietatis, atque integritatis laude floruerunt. Quae quidem Romana Curia ab istis adulatoribus composita, quamuis hodie regnare videatur, nunquam tamen regni sui vires ante Concilium Tridentinum stabilire potuit. Isti sunt, qui ex nobis quaerere solent, ubi fuerat Ecclesia nostra ante Martinum Lutherum? Respondemus, nos esse in Ecclesia illa, quae sancta est, quae una est in partibus fi-liisque, cuius Caput est Christus, cuius membra sunt sancti, cuius regula est regula fidei in sacris Scripturis tradita. Possumus etiam istos interrogare, ubi fuerat Ecclesia ipsorum ante Concilium Tridentinum? Et quis est ex omni adulatorum & fratercu-lorum colluvie, qui ad hanc interrogationem respondere possit? Nos enim confidenter asserimus, & per Dei gratiam veritatem quaerentibus probaturos nos, imo jam probasse confidimus, Ecclesiam illam, quam unicam Jesuitæ probant, & venerantur, cuius Caput est Romanus Pontifex, cuius membra sunt homines sine ulla interna virtute, cuius regula non sit regula fidei in solis Scripturis tradita, sed Romanæ traditiones non scriptæ: non esse Ecclesiam illam unicam, quam suo sanguine redemit Christus, quam instituerunt Apostoli, quam retinuerunt Patres, quæ victrix contra mundum, & Antichristum, contra vitia & hæreses ad finem usque mundi est duratura, & in æternum cum Christo regnatura: sed esse synagogam ab Ecclesia diversam, quæ nec antiquitatem ante exortos fraterculorum ordines, nec auctoritatem ante Concilii Tridentini tempora ostendere possit.
units.tr: We answer: this is what we have already taught, namely that the Roman Church is one thing and the Roman Curia another. The Roman Church has often set itself against the Pope and the Roman Curia. And although that Roman Curia, having conquered in the end together with the Pope, seems to have trampled the Church underfoot, yet let them recognise their origin: this low and ignoble race of men, compounded of the old little friars, the recent Jesuits, and other flatterers, which only lately became known to the world, has always been rejected by the Church and condemned by those who flourished in the Roman Church with a reputation for learning, piety and integrity. This Roman Curia, put together by these flatterers, though today it seems to reign, could never establish the strength of its rule before the Council of Trent. These are the people who are accustomed to ask us: where was your Church before Martin Luther? We reply that we are in that Church which is holy, which is one in its parts and members, whose Head is Christ, whose members are the saints, and whose rule is the rule of faith delivered in the holy Scriptures. We may also ask them: where was their Church before the Council of Trent? And who, out of the whole crowd of flatterers and little friars, can answer this question? For we confidently assert, and by the grace of God we will prove to those who seek the truth, indeed we are confident that we have already proved, that the Church which the Jesuits alone approve and venerate, whose Head is the Roman Pontiff, whose members are men without any inward virtue, and whose rule is not the rule of faith delivered in the Scriptures alone, but unwritten Roman traditions, is not that one Church which Christ redeemed with his blood, which the Apostles founded, which the Fathers preserved, which, victorious over the world and Antichrist, over vices and heresies, is to endure until the end of the world and reign with Christ for ever; rather it is a synagogue distinct from the Church, which can show neither an antiquity older than the rise of the orders of the little friars, nor an authority older than the time of the Council of Trent.

units.la: TERTIA CONTROVERSIA. DE FIDE IUSTIFICANTE.
units.tr: THIRD CONTROVERSY. ON JUSTIFYING FAITH.

units.la: THESES PONTIFICIÆ.
units.tr: THE PAPAL THESES.

units.la: Si quis dixerit, sola fide impium iustificari, ut intelligat nihil aliud requiri, quod ad iustificationis gratiam consequendam cooperetur, & nulla ex parte necesse esse, cum sua voluntatis motu[?] præparari, atque disponi, anathema sit. Concil. Trident. sessio. 6. can.9.
units.tr: If anyone shall say that the impious man is justified by faith alone, so that he understands that nothing else is required which cooperates in obtaining the grace of justification, and that in no way is it necessary for him to be prepared and disposed by the movement of his own will, let him be anathema. Council of Trent, session 6, canon 9.

units.la: Si quis dixerit, homines iustificari, vel sola imputatione iustitiae Christi, vel sola peccatorum remissione, exclusa gratia & charitate, quae in cordibus eorum per Spiritum S. diffunditur, atque illis inhaeret: aut etiam gratiam qua iustificamur esse tantum modo fauorem Dei, anathema sit. Concil. Tridentin. sessione 6. can. 11.
units.tr: If anyone shall say that men are justified either by the sole imputation of the righteousness of Christ, or by the sole remission of sins, with grace and charity excluded, which is poured out in their hearts by the Holy Spirit and inheres in them; or that the grace by which we are justified is only the favour of God, let him be anathema. Council of Trent, session 6, canon 11.

units.la: CAPUT I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Quaestionis [?]status atque exponitur.
units.tr: The state of the question, and its explanation.

units.la: Post sacrarum scripturarum, & Ecclesiae ca-tholicae tractationem, sequitur, ut quaera-mus de fide iustificante, quae est ecclesiae vita. Quaestio non est, an opera sint necessaria: in eo mutuus consensus agnoscitur. Sed de iustificatione impii in conspectu Dei, sive de remissione peccatorum, & imputatione iustitiae Christi controversia fit. Quum enim docemus, iustificari hominem coram Deo sola fide, sine operibus, vel ex congruo, per praepa-rationes, & dispositiones (de quibus prior capitulum non loquitur) vel ex condigno, per modum habitus meritibus: modum iustificationis de-claramus in imputatione iustitiae Christi, & non imputatis peccatis nostris. Haec iustitia non est nobis inhaerens, sed donata a Deo, accepta autem au-tem sola fide, quia quum Deus iustificat impium, nulla opera in impio videre potest, nisi impia. Itaque sicut testatur Apostolus, com-mendat suam erga nos charitatem Deus, eo quod, quum adhuc essemus peccatores, Christus pro nobis mor-tuus est. eius est, iustificati igitur nunc eius sanguine seruabi-mur multo magis per illum ab ira, nam si quum inimici essemus reconciliati fuimus Deo per mortem fi-lii eius, multo magis reconciliati seruabimur per vitam ipsius. Christus enim, sicut idem Apostolus docet, quum nulli adhuc viribus essemus, suo tem-pore pro impiis mortuus est: hæc Apostolus.
units.tr: After the treatment of Holy Scripture and of the catholic Church, we come to ask about justifying faith, which is the life of the Church. The question is not whether good works are necessary; on that point there is common agreement. The controversy concerns the justification of the sinner before God, that is, the remission of sins and the imputation of the righteousness of Christ. When we teach that a man is justified before God by faith alone, without works, whether by congruous merit through preparations and dispositions (about which the earlier chapter does not speak), or by condign merit through a habit of merit, we are declaring the manner of justification to lie in the imputation of Christ's righteousness and in our sins not being imputed to us. This righteousness is not inherent in us but is given to us by God, and it is received by faith alone, because when God justifies the ungodly he can see in the ungodly no works except ungodly ones. Therefore, as the Apostle testifies: "God commends his love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if when we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. For Christ, as the same Apostle teaches, when we were still without strength, died in due time for the ungodly." So says the Apostle.

units.la: Vbi iam sunt præparationes, & dispositiones nostræ à Tridentinis iactatæ? Si enim reconciliati sumus Deo, atque iustificati, quum nullis iam viribus essemus ad promerendum Deum, imo vero quum peccatores essemus, quum impii, quum inimici (quæ omnia diserte Apostoli verbis continentur) profecto sola Dei charitas, sola gratia eò me datur nobis, solus Fan or[?] ille, cui Concil. Trid. anathema dicit.
units.tr: Where, then, are the preparations and dispositions of ours that the Tridentines boast of? For if we are reconciled to God and justified, when we had no strength left to deserve God's favour, indeed when we were sinners, ungodly and enemies (all of which are plainly contained in the Apostle's words), then surely it is God's love alone, grace alone, and that favour alone, which is given to us, and which the Council of Trent curses with anathema.

units.la: Præparationes ad iustificationem non negamus quidem, sed dicimus esse præparationes istas non à nobis, sed in nobis à Deo. Et so-phistas Tridentinos in eo maxime errare, qui e Scotistarum lacunis docent, istas præparationes esse ex motu voluntaris, vel, vt loquitur Scotus, ex puris naturalibus, per quas mereri potest homo gratiam primam, quam vocant. Quid hoc aliud est, quàm quod docuit Pelagius: gratiam dari secundum merita nostra, quæ sententia in Pelagio damnata, ab Augustino atq; ab Ecclesia vniuersa reiecta, tandem per Scotistas revixit, & in Concilio Tridentino promulgata, & tanquam Christianæ fidei fundamentum firmata fuit. Nos cum Augustino docemus, istas etiam præparationes à Deo esse, atq; ex gratia. {a}Quomodo, inquit ille, non volentis neq; currentis, sed miserentis Dei, nisi quia & ipsa voluntas, sicut scriptum est, à Deo praeparatur? Alioquin sic propterea dicitur: non volentis neque currentis, sed miserentis Dei, quia ex utroque fit, id est, ex voluntate hominis, & misericordia Dei, tanquam diceretur, non sufficit sola voluntas hominis, si non sit etiam misericordia Dei: ergo non sufficit sola misericordia Dei, si non sit etiam voluntas hominis. Haec quum Augustinus varie, ut solet, versat [?] & pertractat, ut veritas ex luculenti tractatione magis elucear, tandem sic concludit: restat ut propterea dictum intelligatur: non volentis, neque currentis, sed miserentis Dei, ut totum Deo detur, qui hominis voluntatem bonam, & praeparat adiuuando, & adiuuat praeparatam.
units.tr: We do not deny that there are preparations for justification, but we say that these preparations are not from us but in us, from God. And the Tridentine sophists err most of all in this, that they teach from the puddles of the Scotists that these preparations come from the movement of the will, or, as Scotus puts it, from purely natural powers, by which man can merit the first grace, as they call it. What is this other than what Pelagius taught: that grace is given according to our merits? That opinion was condemned in Pelagius, rejected by Augustine and by the whole Church, yet at last it revived through the Scotists and was promulgated in the Council of Trent and confirmed as the foundation of the Christian faith. We, with Augustine, teach that these preparations too are from God and are of grace. "How," he says, "is it not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy, unless because the will itself, as it is written, is prepared by God? Otherwise it would not be said, 'not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy', because it comes from both, that is, from the will of man and the mercy of God, as if it were said: the will of man is not sufficient alone unless there is also the mercy of God; therefore the mercy of God alone is not sufficient unless there is also the will of man." When Augustine, as is his custom, has turned this over in various ways and worked it through, so that the truth may shine forth more clearly from this lucid treatment, he at last concludes thus: "It remains that it is to be understood as said: not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy, so that the whole is given to God, who both prepares the good will of man by helping, and helps the will once prepared."

units.la: Hæc ille, quibus verbis manifeste probat, omnes istas praeparationes ex gratia esse, ut totum Deo detur, qui hominis voluntatem bonam, & praeparat adiuuando, & adiuuat praeparatam. Ergo Tridentini, qui hominem ex se suæ voluntatis motu praeparari, atque disponi docent, totum Deo dare non possunt, cum Ecclesiæ patribus: sed cum Pelagio, partem Deo, partem sibi.
units.tr: So he says, and by these words he plainly proves that all these preparations are from grace, so that the whole is given to God, who both prepares the good will of man by helping, and helps the will once prepared. Therefore the Tridentines, who teach that man is prepared and disposed of himself by the movement of his own will, cannot give the whole to God along with the Fathers of the Church; they give part to God and part to themselves, with Pelagius.

units.la: Qui negant, ad iustificationem impij satis esse peccatorum remissionem, & impurationem iustitiæ Christi, propterea obtrudunt opera, quod intelligere nolunt, quomodo iustitia Christi facta sit nostra. Quum igitur de solius fidei iustificatione disputamus, consilium est, iustitiam Dei, qua sola iustificatur impius, aperire, non propriam: impuratione miseri-corditer corditer concessam & donatam dum habitus inhærietem[?]; sola f[illegible, ~3 letters] non operibus nostris partam, prauitas,& hæresis reuincatur, [illegible, ~2 letters] nes nostras & præparationes, n[illegible, ~3 letters] tra Apostolum statuit, & chari[illegible, ~3 letters] uoremque, tantum, tátopere n[illegible, ~3 letters] ris commendatum pernegat: [illegible, ~2 letters] blasphemantri os obturetur, q[illegible, ~3 letters] mali causa iustificationis dispu[illegible, ~4 letters] confirmare iustitiam inhærentem iustitiæ Christi, vt eam penitus utilem reiicere videatur. sic enim iustitia inhærens sit formalis cau[illegible, ~3 letters] (quod decent Pontifices) non requiri iustitia Christi, quæ iustificationem tam, & imperfectam absolvat. H[illegible, ~2 letters] mum est, quod alicubi Nazia[nzenus?] neminem de Spiritu sancto re[?] sine Spiritu sancto. Itaque non [illegible, ~2 letters] suitæ, tanquam bofpites, & pe[?] steris fidei nostræ loquantur, [illegible, ~2 letters] gratia iustificationis & sanctif[?] disputare potest, nisi qui gratiam vt igitur blasphemiæ istæ veritat[?] tur, è scripturis patribusque im[?] solius fidei doctrinam confirma[?]
units.tr: Those who deny that the remission of sins and the imputation of the righteousness of Christ are enough for the justification of the sinner, press works upon us for this reason, that they are unwilling to understand how the righteousness of Christ has become ours. Therefore, since we dispute about justification by faith alone, our purpose is to set forth the righteousness of God, by which the sinner alone is justified, and not our own; a righteousness mercifully granted and given by imputation, not obtained by our works. Thus the perversity and heresy are refuted… [the author's argument turns against those who would make an inherent righteousness the formal cause of justification, and against those who deny that the righteousness of Christ is needed to absolve the imperfect; as Gregory of Nazianzus says somewhere, no one speaks rightly of the Holy Spirit without the Holy Spirit]. So that these blasphemies may be silenced, and the mouths of those who dispute about justification as though it were a matter of works… [the author promises to confirm the doctrine of faith alone from Scripture and the Fathers].

units.la: CAPVT II. Iustificationis doctrina ex scripturis probatur. [illegible, ~6 letters]
units.tr: CHAPTER II. The doctrine of justification is proved from Scripture. [illegible]

units.la: DVo iustitiæ genera propo[illegible, ~5 letters] pruris: iustitia Dei, & iu[?] n, non per mo-ide prensatam, vt Tridentina quæ dispositio-neritorias con-tatem Dei, fa-obis in scriptu-[?]ac Bellarmino qui cum de for-ret, coneturque em, ira insultat, tamquam in-m scribit : {a}si si iustificationis ritur imputatio alioquin incho-ac ille. Verisi-inzenus[?] habet, se[?] loqui posse, miramur, si le-regrini[?] de my-nemo enim de icationis recte n illam habeat, tis luce diffipe-putationis, & abimus.

Nazianzen ... has, ... we can speak, we marvel, if ... [illegible] ... for no one ... of justification rightly ... has it, ... [illegible] ... the light of imputation, and we depart.

units.la: la fide, pro-nuntur in scri-iustitia operum, prima dicitur Iustitia Dei Rom. 1. 17. Iustitia Dei per illud (Euangelium) revelatur ex fide in fidem. Sic passim. Haec eadem dicitur etiam iustitia fidei Rom. 4. 11. Et signum accepit circumcisionis, signaculum iustitiae fidei, & Rom. 11. 6. quae ex fide est iustitia. Nonnunquam appellationes istae connectuntur, & dicitur iustitia Dei per fidem. Iustitia Dei per fidem omnes, & super omnes credentes.
units.tr: by faith, pro-nounced in the Scriptures, the righteousness of works, the first is called the Righteousness of God Rom. 1.17. The righteousness of God is revealed through that (Gospel) from faith to faith. So throughout. This same thing is also called the righteousness of faith, Rom. 4.11: "And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of faith," and Rom. 11.6: "which is of faith, is righteousness." Sometimes these expressions are joined, and it is called the righteousness of God through faith: the righteousness of God through faith in all, and upon all who believe.

units.la: Alia est iustitia operum, eademq; vocatur iustitia legis; quia Lex opera requirit. Moses describit iustitiam quae ex lege est. Haec eadem etiam propria iustitia appellatur, de qua sic Apostolus: non habe[?] iustitiam meam, quae est ex lege, sed eam, quae est per fidem Christi, id est, iustitiam quae ex Deo est per fidem. Haec Apostolus, atque alio loco, vtrum Iudaeos an Pontificios rectius describant[?], iudicet Lector: Ignorantes, inquit, iustitiam Dei, & propriam iustitiam studentes constituere, iustitiae Dei non fuerunt subiecti.
units.tr: The other is the righteousness of works, and it is likewise called the righteousness of the law, because the Law requires works. Moses describes the righteousness which is of the law. This same righteousness is also called one's own righteousness, of which the Apostle speaks thus: not having my own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, that is, the righteousness which is of God through faith. So the Apostle; and in another place, let the reader judge whether the Jews or the Papists are described more correctly: Being ignorant, he says, of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to the righteousness of God.

units.la: Haec ita tractat sacra scriptura, vt à iustificatione nostri semper excludatur iustitia operum, quae est eadem iustitia legis, eademq; iustitia nostra propria. Fide iustificatis absque operibus, vt iustificemur ex fide, non ex operibus legis. Iustitia Dei sine lege; non ex vobis[?] ipsis, Dei donum est, non ex operibus, ne quis glorietur, non habens iustitiam meam, quae ex lege est, ignorantes iustitiam Dei, & propriam iustitiam studentes constituere, iustitiae Dei non fuerunt subiecti.
units.tr: Holy Scripture treats it in such a way that the righteousness of works, which is the same as the righteousness of the law and the same as our own proper righteousness, is always excluded from our justification: justified by faith apart from works, so that we may be justified by faith and not by the works of the law. The righteousness of God without the law; not from yourselves, it is the gift of God, not from works, lest anyone should boast; not having my own righteousness, which is of the law; being ignorant of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to the righteousness of God.

units.la: nem in in fide statui, vt nullus locus operibus nostris, aut iustitiæ nostræ propriæ, inhærenti nobis relinquatur: fidem esse donum Dei: nec tamen quod ius Donum Dei ad iustitiam Dei excipiendam idoneum esse, sed illud donum, quod omnem gloriationem excludat: fidem omnem gloriationem nostram excludere: opera igitur, quamuis sint etiam ipsa donum Dei, idcirco tamen à iustificando reiecta, quia non excludunt omnem gloriationem: non ex vobis ipsis, non ex operibus, ne quis glorietur itemque [illegible, ~8 letters] est gloriatio: [illegible, ~10 letters] per quam le- gem quærunt nos, sed per legem fidei. Quid hæc aliud volunt, nisi, ut omnibus operibus exclusis, non in nobis sed in domino gloriemur, ad impium iustificandum Dei misericordiam relinquatur. Nullam igitur aliam iustificationem impii fecerunt tradunt licere, præter unicam illam, qua opera excluduntur. Dicitur enim iustitia Dei sicta nostra, & Christus à Deo factus nobis iustitia, modus quo fit, dicitur imputatio, manuque excipitur, fides, fides autem sola excipere dicitur hanc iustificationem, quia nihil est in homine, præter fidem, quod vel conspectum Dei ferre posset, vel gloriationem omnem abiicere. Hi- des enim reiecta omni gloriatione nostra, vnicum Deum in Christo placatum nobis, nec quicquam proprium, tanquam necessarium ad iustificationem respicit. Hæc veritas ita fir- ma, solida, adeoque tuta est, vt etiam ex ore quorumcunque hostium testimonium extorquetur.
units.tr: ...in faith, so that no place is left in us for our works, or for our own righteousness, inhering in us: faith is a gift of God, yet not because faith is a gift of God is it fit to receive the righteousness of God, but because it is a gift which excludes all boasting: faith excludes all our boasting, therefore works, although they too are gifts of God, are for that reason rejected from justifying, because they do not exclude all boasting: "not from yourselves, not from works, lest anyone should boast," and likewise [illegible] ... is boasting: [illegible] ... by which they seek us through the law, but through the law of faith. What do these things mean, other than that, with all works excluded, we should glory not in ourselves but in the Lord, and that the mercy of God is left to justify the ungodly? They therefore taught that no other justification of the ungodly is lawful, except that single one in which works are excluded. For the righteousness of God is called our righteousness, and Christ made by God our righteousness; the manner by which it happens is called imputation, and it is received by hand, which is faith; and faith alone is said to receive this justification, because there is nothing in man, besides faith, which could bear the sight of God or cast off all boasting. For faith, having rejected all our boasting, looks to the one God who is reconciled to us in Christ, and to nothing of our own as necessary for justification. This truth is so firm, solid and secure that it is wrung even from the mouths of whatever enemies.

units.la: Cardinalis Bellarminus, postquam eam multis verbis oppugnauerit, tandem tamen testatur, id ab eo agi, quodammodo reclamante conscientia. Sic enim scribit: {a}Propter incertitudinem propriæ iustitiæ, & periculum inanis gloriæ, tutissimum est, fiduciam totam in sola Dei misericordia, & benignitate reponere. hæc ille. Quod ergo Apostolus Paulus docuit, non ex operibus, ne quis glorietur, Bellarminus illud quidem tutissimum esse fatetur, propter inanis gloriæ periculum. Apage cum illis tepidis commentis, si tutissimum est, quod de fide tradit Apostolus, profecto verissimum etiam erit. Nihil enim tutum de fide esse potest, nisi quia verum est. Miseri ergo Tridentini omnes, miseri Iesuitæ sua confessione inveniuntur, qui ex præscripto Tridentino tutissimam fidei doctrinam relinquunt, ut reiecta iustitia Dei, propriam iusticiam constituant.
units.tr: Cardinal Bellarmine, after he has assailed it with many words, at last nevertheless bears witness that he does this in some measure against the protest of his conscience. For he writes thus: {a}On account of the uncertainty of one's own righteousness, and the danger of empty glory, it is safest to place all confidence in the mercy and goodness of God alone. So he. Therefore what the Apostle Paul taught, not from works, lest anyone should boast, Bellarmine concedes is indeed the safest, on account of the danger of empty glory. Away with those lukewarm inventions! If what the Apostle teaches about faith is safest, it will certainly also be most true. For nothing about faith can be safe unless it is true. Wretched therefore are all the Tridentines, wretched are the Jesuits, who are found by their own confession, who by the Tridentine prescription leave aside the safest doctrine of faith, so that, rejecting the righteousness of God, they establish their own righteousness.

units.la: Quod obiiciunt pontificii verba Iacobi Apostoli: Respondemus, Iacobum nullo modo Paulo contradicere. Paulus docet, hominem non operibus, sed fide iustificari, Iacobus non fide sola, sed operibus; utrque Apostolus Abrahami factum producit in exemplum, nonne igitur est contradictio? Aliud minus, nam contradictio nulla esse potest, nisi omnes termini accipiantur συνωνύμως[?]. In hac autem propositione, fide homo iustificatur, duplex est homonymia, una in verbo, iustificari: altera in verbo, fide. Iustificari enim aliquis dicitur coram Deo, sicut impius iustificatur, de qua fighificatione iustificationis Paulus loquitur, non autem Iacobus, nam sanctus Paulus docet, nos iustificatos Christi sanguine, quū iam essemus nullis viribus, quumque essemus peccatores, impii, atque inimici. Loquitur ergo de iustificatione impii coram Deo, quum peccata nobis propter Christum condonantur: non propter nostra merita, nam quale meritum esse posset iniis qui sunt peccatores, impii, inimici Deo, ac proinde nullis viribus, ad fauorem Dei promerendum ex ipsis. At sanctus Iacobus loquitur de ostensione iustitiae, & fidei coram Ecclesia; nam sic ait: ostende mihi fidem tuam. Non ergo loquuntur ad idem. Deinde fides etiam varie sumitur: nam vel fides est vera, viva, iustificans, de qua Paulus agit: vel est historica fides, quae est & dæmo-num, de qua Iacobus; de fide historica Iacobum loqui est extra controversiam, ex illis verbis: fides, si opera non habeat mortua est, & dæmones credunt, & horrescunt. Quum ergo constet, Iacobum loqui de fide quae potest esse mortua, quae potest esse sine operibus, quae potest esse Dæmonum; certum est, Paulum Iacobumque non de eadem fide locutos esse, ac proinde non inter se contradicentia dixisse. Sic solebant antiqui Apostolorum scripta conciliare. Pontificii vero lepidus videpta conciliare: tur ludus scripturas inter se committere, lutemque tollere, vtpote interim per tenebras effugere possint. Ipse etiam Thom. Aquinas in hanc fere sententiam de his duobus Apostolis stolis disputat. Sic enim scribit: a Iacobus quitur de operibus sequentibus fidem, quæ dicuntur iustificare, non secundum quod iustificare dicitur in- fusio, sed secundum quod dicitur iustificare exercita- tio, vel ostensio, vel consummatio, res enim seriditur, quando perficitur, & innotescit. Haec Aqui-nas. Videmus igitur apud Paulum, & Iacobum, in hac propositione [?] iustificari fide terminos non sumpserunt, utrumque quod verum est dicit, sed non loquuntur ad idem, sed vero de iustificatione hoc loco disputantes, non vt est iustitiæ ostensio coram hominibus, sed vt ex S. Pauli doctrina, coarguit remissio-nem peccatorum, atque imputationem iustitiæ Christi, quam Christiani inputationem resiciunt, tanquam non necessariam, de remissione peccatorum, vel de non imputatis nobis credentibus, peccatum nostrum, plenæ sunt sacræ literæ. Apostolus ex Psalmis profert, Beatitudinem nostram, idest, iustificationem nostram esse in remissione peccatorum. Beati quorum remissæ sunt iniquitates, & quorum tecta sunt peccata. Et qua fides nostra, quæ remissionem peccatorum, & reconciliationem excepit, sine omni merito consistere omnino nequit, idcirco Apostolus fidem, & meritum illud cui fides innititur frequentius coniungit, meritum credentium est, sanguis Christi, idem ergo vult apud Apostolum fide iustificari, & per sanguinem Christi iustificari. Nam qui sola fide se iustificari comm Deo credit, meritum pro-prium
units.tr: As to what the Papists object, the words of the Apostle James: We answer that James in no way contradicts Paul. Paul teaches that a man is justified not by works but by faith; James, not by faith alone but by works; both Apostles bring forward the deed of Abraham as an example. Is there then not a contradiction? Not at all, for there can be no contradiction unless all the terms are taken synonymously [συνωνύμως]. But in this proposition, "a man is justified by faith," there is a twofold equivocation: one in the word justified, the other in the word faith. For someone is said to be justified before God, as the ungodly is justified, and it is of this meaning of justification that Paul speaks, but not James; for the holy Paul teaches that we are justified by the blood of Christ, when we were yet without any strength, and when we were sinners, ungodly, and enemies. He therefore speaks of the justification of the ungodly before God, when sins are forgiven us on account of Christ, not on account of our merits; for what merit could there be in those who are sinners, ungodly, enemies of God, and therefore without any strength to earn favour with God from themselves? But holy James speaks of the showing forth of righteousness and faith before the Church; for he says: "Show me your faith." They therefore do not speak to the same point. Further, faith is also taken in various ways: for either faith is true, living, justifying, of which Paul treats, or it is historical faith, which is also that of demons, of which James speaks. That James speaks of historical faith is beyond controversy, from those words: "faith, if it has no works, is dead," and "the demons believe and shudder." Since it is therefore clear that James speaks of a faith which can be dead, which can be without works, which can be that of demons, it is certain that Paul and James did not speak of the same faith, and consequently did not say things contradicting each other. Thus the ancients used to reconcile the writings of the Apostles. But the Papists, in a wretched game, set the Scriptures against one another and remove the knot, since in the meantime they can escape through the darkness. Thomas Aquinas himself, to about this effect, disputes concerning these two Apostles. For he writes thus: James speaks of the works following faith, which are said to justify, not according as justifying means infusion, but according as it means the exercise, or the showing forth, or the consummation; for a thing is perfected and becomes known when it is completed. So Aquinas. We see therefore that in Paul and James, in this proposition "justified by faith," they did not take the terms in the same way; each says what is true, but they do not speak to the same point. Rather, disputing here about justification, not as it is a showing forth of righteousness before men, but as, according to the doctrine of St. Paul, it concerns the remission of sins and the imputation of the righteousness of Christ, which the Christians of that imputation deny as unnecessary, the sacred letters are full of the remission of sins, and of the non-imputation of our sin to us who believe. The Apostle quotes from the Psalms that our blessedness, that is, our justification, consists in the remission of sins: Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. And since our faith, which received remission of sins and reconciliation, cannot at all stand without any merit, the Apostle therefore frequently joins faith and that merit on which faith rests: the merit of believers is the blood of Christ. So he means among the Apostles both to be justified by faith and to be justified through the blood of Christ. For he who believes that he is justified before God by faith alone, his own merit...
